The meaning of offspring in the speech of the Arabs is known to be the descendants of those to whom they were attributed before, men and women, as God Almighty said: The descendants of those We carried with Noah (al-Isra’ 17:3), and as He said: And among his descendants were David, Solomon, Job, and Joseph, then He said after: And Zachariah, John, Jesus, and Elias (al-An’am 6:84, 85), so He made those who were before men and women from the descendants of Abraham. As for his saying: and their chiefs, “chiefs” are the nobles. The interpretation of the statement is: out of fear of Pharaoh and their chiefs. The Arabists differed as to who was meant by the ha and meem in his statement: and their chiefs.

Some of the grammarians of Basra said: He meant the offspring. It is as if he directed the speech to: And none believed in Moses except a few offspring from his people, out of fear of Pharaoh, and the chiefs were the offspring of the Children of Israel. Some grammarians of Kufa said: By them he meant Pharaoh. He said: This is permissible, and Pharaoh is one, because when a king is mentioned in fear, travel, or returning from a journey, the imagination goes to him and to those with him. He said: Don’t you see that you say: (The caliph arrived and the people increased), meaning those with him, (and he arrived and prices rose), because you mean by his arrival the arrival of those with him. He said: It may be that by (Pharaoh) you mean the family of Pharaoh, and you delete (the family), so it is permissible as he said: And ask the town
r
(Yusuf 12:82)
, meaning the people of the town, and God knows best.
He said: Similar to it is his saying: O Prophet, when you divorce women, divorce them during their waiting period (al-Talaq 65:1).

The most correct of the sayings in this regard, in my opinion, is the saying of those who said: (The ha and the mim) refer to (the offspring), and the meaning of the statement is that he is in fear of Pharaoh and the chiefs of the offspring, because there were among the offspring of the century to whom he was sent those whose father was Coptic and whose mother was Israelite. So whoever was like that among them, was with Pharaoh against Moses. His saying: that he might tempt them, means: The faith of those who believed from the descendants of Moses’ people was out of fear of Pharaoh, that he might tempt them with punishment, turning them away from their religion, and causing them to turn back from their faith and disbelieve in God. He said: That he might tempt them, so he used the singular form, and did not say: that he might tempt them, because of the evidence of the report about Pharaoh in this regard: that his people were in the same state as he was in, because of what had been mentioned previously in his statement: in fear of Pharaoh and his chiefs.

And His statement: And indeed, Pharaoh was arrogant in the land, God Almighty says: And indeed, Pharaoh was a tyrant, arrogant towards God in his land, and indeed, he was among the transgressors, and indeed, he was among those who transgressed the truth towards falsehood, and that was his disbelief in God, and his abandonment of belief in Him, and his denial of the oneness of God, and his claim for himself to be a god, and his shedding of blood unlawfully.

God Almighty says, informing about what His Prophet Moses said to his al-Nas 114:O my people, if you have acknowledged the Oneness of God and believed in His Lordship, then put your trust in Him, meaning: So trust in Him, and submit to His command, for He will not let down His guardian, and he who puts his trust in Him will not be safe, if you are Muslims, meaning: If you are obedient to God, then put your trust in Him.
God Almighty says: The people of Moses said to Moses: In God we trust, meaning: We trust in Him, and to Him we entrust our affairs. And His saying: Our Lord,
h
do not make us a trial for the wrongdoing people

, God Almighty says, informing about the people of Moses: that they called upon their Lord and said: O our Lord, do not test these disbelieving people and do not try them with us, meaning the people of Pharaoh.
The people of interpretation differed regarding the meaning that they asked their Lord for, of His protection from the affliction of Pharaoh’s people with them.

Some of them said: They asked him not to make them prevail over them, lest they think that they were better than them, and that they were only given power over them because of their dignity in his eyes and the humiliation of others.
Who said that?

c: Ibn Wakee’ told us, he said, my father told us, on the authority of Imran bin Hudayr, on the authority of Abu Majlaz,
m: regarding his statement: Our Lord,
h
do not make us a trial for the wrongdoing people
, he said: So that they do not prevail over us, so that they see themselves as better than us.

c: Al-Muthanna told me, he said, Al-Hajjaj told us, he said, Hammad told us, on the authority of Imran bin Hudayr, on the authority of Abu Majlaz,
m: regarding his statement: Our Lord,
h
do not make us a trial for the wrongdoing people
, he said: They said: Do not make them prevail over us, so that they see that they are better than us.

c: Ibn Wakee’ told us, he said, my father told us, on the authority of Sufyan, on the authority of his father, on the authority of Abu Ad-Dahha:
m: Our Lord,
h
do not make us a trial for the wrongdoing people
, he said: Do not give them power over us, so that they become more tempted.

x: Others said: Rather, the meaning of this is: Do not let them rule over us so that they tempt us.
Who said that?

c: Ibn Wakee’ told us, he said, Ibn Uyaynah told us, on the authority of Ibn Abi Nujayh, on the authority of Mujahid:
m: h
Do not make us a trial for the wrongdoing people
, do not give them power over us so that they tempt us.

c: Al-Muthanna told me, he said, Ishaq told us, he said, Abdullah bin Al-Zubayr told us, on the authority of Ibn Uyaynah, on the authority of Ibn Abi Nujayh, on the authority of Mujahid,
m: regarding his statement: Our Lord,
h
do not make us a trial for the wrongdoing people
, he said: Do not give them power over us so that they lead us astray.

c: Al-Hasan bin Yahya told us, he said: Abd al-Razzaq told us, he said: Ibn Uyaynah told us, on the authority of Ibn Abi Nujayh, on the authority of Mujahid,
m: the same, and he also said: They tempt us.

c: Al-Muthanna told me, he said, Abu Hudhayfah told us, he said, Shibl told us, on the authority of Ibn Abi Nujayh, on the authority of Mujahid:
m: h
Do not make us a trial for the wrongdoing people

, do not punish us at the hands of Pharaoh’s people, nor with a punishment from You, so that Pharaoh’s people say: If they were right, we would not have been given power over them nor would they have been punished, so that they would be tempted by us.

c: Al-Qasim told us, he said, Al-Husayn told us, he said, Hajjaj told me, on the authority of Ibn Jurayj, on the authority of Mujahid,
m: regarding his statement:
h
Do not make us a trial for the wrongdoing people

, he said: Do not punish us at the hands of Pharaoh’s people or with a punishment from you, so that Pharaoh’s people say: If they were on the right path, we would not have been given power over them or punished, so that they would be tempted by us.

c: Ibn Hamid told us, he said, Hakam told us, on the authority of Anbasa, on the authority of Muhammad ibn Abd al-Rahman, on the authority of al-Qasim ibn Abi Bazza, on the authority of Mujahid,
m: regarding his statement:
h
Do not make us a trial for the wrongdoing people

, he said: Do not afflict us with a punishment from You or by their hands, so that they are tempted and say: If they were on the right path, We would not have been given power over them and they would not have been punished.

c: Yunus told me: Ibn Wahb told us: Ibn Zayd said
m: about His statement: Our Lord, make us not a trial for the wrongdoing people, “Do not test us, our Lord, and exhaust us, and make it a trial for them, this trial.” And he recited: A trial for the wrongdoing people (37:63), he said: The polytheists, when they used to harm the Prophet, may God bless him and his family and grant them peace, and the believers and throw stones at them, was that not a trial and evil for them, while it is a calamity for the believers?

x: The correct thing to say about that is that the people asked God to protect them from being a trial and a calamity for the people of Pharaoh. Everything that happened was a deterrent for them from following Moses and acknowledging him and what he brought to them. There is no doubt that it was a trial for them, and it was one of the greatest things that distanced them from faith in God and His Messenger. Likewise, one of the deterrents to faith was that if the people of Moses were suddenly a trial from God in themselves, from a calamity that would befall them, then the people sought refuge with God from every meaning that would prevent the people of Pharaoh from faith in God due to their causes.

God Almighty says: And save us, O our Lord, by Your mercy, so deliver us from the hands of the disbelieving people, the people of Pharaoh, because they were enslaving them and using them in the dirty things of their service.
God Almighty says:
h
And We inspired Moses and his brother

, saying, Build houses for your people in Egypt. It is said: So-and-so made a house for himself, if he took it. Likewise: He made a house for himself, if he took it, And I made it a house for him, if he took it for himself.
h
And make your homes places of prayer
, meaning: And make your homes mosques in which you pray.
The interpreters differed in their interpretation of his saying:
h
And make your homes places of prayer
Some of them said something similar to what we said about it.
Who said that?

c: Ibn Wakee’ told us, he said, my father told us, on the authority of Sufyan, on the authority of Hameed, on the authority of Ikrimah, on the authority of Ibn Abbas:
m: h
And make your houses places of prayer
, he said: mosques.

c: Al-Muthanna told me, he said, Abu Naim told us, he said, Sufyan told us, on the authority of Khasif, on the authority of Ikrimah, on the authority of Ibn Abbas,
m: regarding his statement:
h
And make your houses places of prayer

, he said: They were commanded to make them mosques. ... He said, Abu Ghassan Malik bin Ismail told us, he said, Zuhair told us, he said, Khasif told us, on the authority of Ikrimah, on the authority of Ibn Abbas, regarding the statement of God:
h
And make your houses places of prayer
, he said: They were afraid of Pharaoh and his people praying, so he said to them: (Make your houses places of prayer), meaning: Make them a mosque so that you may pray in them.

c: Ibn Wakee’ and Ibn Hamid told us, they said, Jarir told us, on the authority of Mansur, on the authority of Ibrahim:
m: h
And make your houses places of prayer
, he said: They were afraid, so they were ordered to pray in their houses.

c: Ibn Wakee’ told us, he said, my father told us, on the authority of Sufyan, on the authority of Mansur, on the authority of Ibrahim:
m: h
And make your houses places of prayer
. He said: They were afraid, so they were ordered to pray in their houses.

c: Al-Muthanna told me, he said, Al-Hammani told us, he said, Shabl told us, on the authority of Khasif, on the authority of Ikrimah, on the authority of Ibn Abbas,
m: regarding his statement:
h
And make your houses places of prayer
, he said: They were afraid, so they were ordered to pray in their houses.

c: Ibn Wakee’ told us, he said, Ibn Uyaynah told us, on the authority of Ibn Abi Nujayh, on the authority of Mujahid:
m: h
And make your homes places of prayer

. He said: They did not pray except in the shops, and they did not pray except in fear, so they were commanded to pray in their homes. .. He said, Jarir told us, on the authority of Laith, on the authority of Mujahid, who said: They were afraid, so they were ordered to pray in their homes. .. He said, Abdullah told us, on the authority of Israel, on the authority of Al-Suddi, on the authority of Abu Malik:
h
And make your houses places of prayer
, he said: The Children of Israel feared Pharaoh, so they were commanded to make their houses mosques in which to pray.

c: Al-Muthanna told me, he said, Ishaq told us, he said, Abd al-Rahman ibn Saʿd told us, he said, Abu Jaʿfar told us, on the authority of al-Rabiʿ ibn Anas,
m: regarding his statement:
h
And make your houses places of prayer
, he said: mosques. .. He said, Ahmad bin Yunus told us, he said, Israel told us, on the authority of Mansour, on the authority of Ibrahim:
h
And make your houses places of prayer
, he said: They used to pray in their houses, fearing.

c: Ibn Wakee’ told us, he said, Zaid bin Al-Habbab told us, on the authority of Abu Sinan, on the authority of Al-Dahhak:
m: That you provide houses for your people in Egypt, he said: mosques.

c: Ibn Bashar told us, he said, Abd al-Rahman told us, he said, Sufyan told us, on the authority of Mansur, on the authority of Ibrahim,
m: regarding his statement:
h
And make your houses places of prayer
, he said: They were afraid, so they were ordered to pray in their houses.

c: Yunus told me, he said, Ibn Wahb told us, he said: Ibn Zayd said
m: regarding His statement:
h
And make your houses places of prayer
, he said: My father said: Make your houses your mosques in which you pray, that is (the qibla).

x: Others said: Make your mosques before the Kaaba.
Who said that?

c: Ibn Hamid told us, he said, Hakam told us, on the authority of Muhammad ibn Abd al-Rahman ibn Abi Laila, on the authority of al-Munhal, on the authority of Saʿid ibn Jubayr, on the authority of Ibn Abbas:
m: h
And make your houses places of prayer
, meaning the Surat Yunus 10:87
h
And We inspired Moses and his brother
, saying, "Settle for your people in Egypt, houses,
h
and make your houses places of prayer
, and establish prayer,
h
and give good tidings to the believers
." Kaʿbah.

c: Muhammad bin Saad told me, he said, my father told me, he said, my uncle told me, he said, my father told me, on the authority of his father, on the authority of Ibn Abbas,
m: regarding his statement:
h
And make your houses places of prayer and establish prayer and give good tidings to the believers

, he said: The Children of Israel said to Moses: We cannot openly pray with the Pharaohs! So God permitted them to pray in their houses, and they were commanded to make their houses places of prayer toward the Qiblah.

c: Al-Qasim told us, Al-Hussein told us, Hajjaj told me, on the authority of Ibn Jurayj, on the authority of Mujahid, who said, Ibn Abbas said
m: regarding His statement: And make your houses places of worship, he said: Direct your houses, (your mosques), toward the qiblah. Do you not see that He says: In houses which God has permitted to be raised (al-Nur 24:36).

c: Ibn Wakee’ told us, he said, Abdullah told us, on the authority of Israel, on the authority of Abu Yahya, on the authority of Mujahid:
m: h
And make your homes places of prayer
, he said: before the prayer.

c: Al-Qasim told us, Al-Hussein told us, Hajjaj told me, on the authority of Ibn Jurayj, on the authority of Mujahid:
m: Your houses are a qiblah, he said: towards the Kaaba, when Moses and those with him feared that Pharaoh would pray in the congregational churches, so they were ordered to make mosques in their houses facing the Kaaba and to pray in them secretly.

c: Al-Muthanna told me, he said, Abu Hudhayfah told us, he said, Shibl told us, on the authority of Ibn Abi Nujayh, on the authority of Mujahid:
m: h
And make your homes places of prayer
, then he mentioned something similar, the same. ... He said, Shabl told us, on the authority of Ibn Abi Nujayh, on the authority of Mujahid:
h
And We inspired Moses and his brother

, saying, ‘Provide houses for your people in Egypt,’ mosques. ... He said, Ishaq told us, Abdullah told us, on the authority of Warqa’, on the authority of Ibn Abi Nujayh, on the authority of Mujahid, regarding his statement:
h
That you establish houses for your people in Egypt
, he said: (Egypt), Alexandria.

c: Bishr bin Muadh told us, he said, Yazid told us, he said, Saeed told us, on the authority of Qatada,
m: regarding his statement: “
h
And We inspired Moses and his brother
, ‘Settle for your people in houses in Egypt
h
and make your houses places of prayer
. ’” He said: That was when Pharaoh prevented them from praying, so they were ordered to make their mosques in their houses, and to face the direction of the qibla.

c: Muhammad bin Abdul A’la told us, he said, Muhammad bin Thawr told us, on the authority of Muammar, on the authority of Qatada:
m: Your houses are a qiblah, he said, towards the qiblah.

c: Wakiʿ told us, he said, Ishaq told us, on the authority of Abu Sinan, on the authority of Ad-Dahhak:
m: h
And We inspired Moses and his brother
, saying, ‘Provide houses for your people in Egypt,’ he said: mosques,
h
and make your houses places of prayer
,’ he said: before the qiblah.

x: Others said: The meaning of this is: Make your houses face each other.
Who said that?

c: Ibn Wakee’ told us, he said, Imran bin Uyaynah told us, on the authority of Ata’, on the authority of Saeed bin Jubair:
m: And make your houses a qiblah, he said: facing one another.

x: The most correct of the sayings on this matter is the one we have already explained, which is that the most common meaning of houses - even though mosques are houses - is inhabited houses, if mentioned by their absolute name, not mosques. Because mosques have a name by which they are known, specific to them, and that is mosques. As for houses in absolute terms without being connected to anything, or added to anything, they are inhabited houses. And also (Qiblah), people mostly use it in the direction of the mosques and for prayers. If this is the case, and it is not permissible to direct the meanings of God’s words except to the most common of their aspects, used by the people of the language in which it was revealed, without the hidden and unknown, unless there is evidence to the contrary, and there is no evidence for His statement:
h
And make your houses places of prayer

, which cuts off the excuse that its meaning is not the apparent one used in the speech of the Arabs, then it is not permissible for us to direct it to other than the apparent one that we have described.
The same applies to his saying, kiss. “And establish prayer,” God Almighty says: And perform the obligatory prayer within its limits and at its times. And His saying:
h
And give good tidings to the believers
, God Almighty says to His Prophet, peace be upon him: And give good tidings to those who establish prayer, who obey God, O Muhammad, the believers, with the great reward from Him.

God Almighty says: And Moses said: O our Lord, You have given Pharaoh and the leaders and nobles of his people - who are the elites - adornment of worldly goods and furnishings, and wealth of gold and silver, in the life of this world, our Lord, that they may go astray from Your way. Moses says to his Lord: Our Lord, You have given them what You have given them of that, so that they may go astray from Your way. There are different readings of this.
Some of them read it as: So that they may lead people astray from Your path, meaning: so that they may lead people astray from Your path and turn them away from Your religion.
Others read it as:
h
So that they may go astray from Your path
, meaning:
h
So that they may go astray from Your path
, and deviate from the path of guidance.

Did God, may He be glorified, give Pharaoh and his people what He gave them of worldly adornments and wealth, in order to lead people astray from His religion - or: in order for them to be led astray from it? If that was the reason He gave them that, then what He gave them was from them for that reason, so there is no blame on them for that?
The meaning of this is different from what you imagined.
The scholars of Arabic differed regarding the meaning of this lam in His statement: li-yidaloo.

Some of the grammarians of Basra said: The meaning of this is: Our Lord, they have strayed from Your path, as He said: So the family of Pharaoh picked him up, that he might become for them an enemy and a cause of grief (al-Qasas 28:8), meaning: So he was for them, and they did not pick him up so that he might become for them an enemy and a cause of grief, but rather they picked him up so that he was for them. He said: This lam comes in this meaning. Some Kufa grammarians said: This lam is lam ki, and the meaning of the statement is: Our Lord, You gave them what You gave them, so that they would go astray, then He invoked against them.

Another said: These lams in His statement: to lead them astray, “to be an enemy to them” (al-Qasas 28:8), and what is similar to them is the interpretation of the khafd: I gave them what I gave them because of their misguidance - and they picked it up because of it - because the situation had come to that. The Arabs make (lam ki) in the meaning of (lam al-khafd) and (lam al-khafd) in the meaning of (lam ki), to make the meaning similar. God Almighty said: They will swear to you by God when you return to them to turn away from them (al-Tawbah 9:95): meaning: because of your turning away, and they did not swear because of their turning away.
You were exalted and you were not worthy of being exalted, but the lost may be afflicted He said: It is only said: (And you were not worthy of the action), and it is not said: (To do), except rarely.
He said: This is from it.

The correct statement in my opinion is that it is lam-ki, and the meaning of the statement is: Our Lord, You gave them what You gave them of the adornments of worldly life and wealth in order to tempt them with it, and to lead Your servants astray from Your path, as a punishment from You. This is as the Most High said: We would have certainly given them abundant water to test them thereby (al-Jinn 72:16-17). And his saying: Our Lord, obliterate their wealth
h
and harden their hearts

, this is a supplication from Moses, he supplicated to God against Pharaoh and his people to change their wealth from its form, and to change it to a state other than the one in which it is, and this is similar to his saying: Before We obliterate faces and turn them back,
r
(An-Nisa’: 47)
, meaning by it: before We change it from the form in which it is. It is said: (He blinded his eye, I blind it, and I blinded it, blinding and blinding).

The Arabs may use (blinding) to mean forgiveness and covering, and to crush and destroy, as Kaʿb ibn Zuhair said: From every freshness of the penis, if it sweats, its display is obscured by the unknown flags The interpreters differed in their interpretation of this in this place.
A group of them said the same thing about it as we said.
Who said that?

c: Zakariya bin Yahra bin Zaida told me, he said, Hajjaj told us, he said, Ibn Jurayj told me, on the authority of Abdullah bin Katheer, he said:
m: It has reached us on the authority of Al-Qurazi regarding his statement: Our Lord, obliterate their wealth, he said: Turn their sugar into stones.

c: Al-Qasim told us, Al-Hussein told us, Hajjaj told me, on the authority of Ibn Jurayj, on the authority of Abdullah bin Katheer, on the authority of Muhammad bin Kaab Al-Qurazi, who said:
m: Make their drunkenness stones.

c: Ibn Wakee’ told us, Yahya bin Yaman told us, on the authority of Abu Jaafar, on the authority of Al-Rabi’, on the authority of Abu Al-Aaliyah:
m: h
Destroy their wealth
, he said: Turn it into stones.

c: Al-Muthanna told me, he said, Abu Hudhayfah told us, he said, Ishaq told us, he said, Abd al-Rahman ibn Saʿd told us, he said, Abu Jaʿfar told us, on the authority of al-Rabiʿ ibn Anas,
m: regarding his statement:
h
Destroy their wealth
, he said: It turned into stones.

c: Bishr told us, he said, Yazid told us, he said, Saeed told us, on the authority of Qatada,
m: regarding his statement: Our Lord, obliterate their wealth, he said: We were informed that their crops were turned into stones.

c: Muhammad bin Abdul A’la told us, he said, Muhammad bin Thawr told us, on the authority of Muammar, on the authority of Qatada:
m: Our Lord, obliterate their wealth, he said: We were informed that their crops had turned into stones.

c: Al-Muthanna told us, Qubaysah bin Uqbah told us, Sufyan told us:
m: Our Lord, obliterate their wealth, he said: They say: It has become stones.

c: Al-Muthanna told me, he said, Ishaq told us, he said, Yahya Al-Hammani told us, he said, Ibn Al-Mubarak told us, on the authority of Ismail, on the authority of Abu Salih,
m: regarding his statement: Our Lord, obliterate their wealth, he said it turned into stones.

c: Al-Hasan bin Yahya told us, he said, Abd al-Razzaq told us, he said, Muammar told us, on the authority of Qatada,
m: regarding his statement: Our Lord, obliterate their wealth, he said: It has reached us that their crops have turned into stones.

c: It was narrated on the authority of Al-Husayn bin Al-Faraj,
m: who said: I heard Abu Muadh, who said: Ubayd bin Sulayman narrated to us, who said: I heard Al-Dahhak say regarding His statement: Our Lord, obliterate their wealth, that God made it into engraved stones in the form in which it was.

c: Yunus told us, he said, Ibn Wahb told us, he said, Ibn Zayd said
m: regarding his statement: Our Lord, obliterate their wealth, he said: He did that, and that happened to them. He obliterated their wealth and it became stones, their gold, their dirhams, their lentils, and everything.

x: Others said: Rather, the meaning of this is: He destroyed it.
Who said that?

c: Zakariya bin Yahya bin Abi Zaida told me, he said, Hajjaj told us, on the authority of Ibn Jurayj, on the authority of Mujahid:
m: Our Lord, obliterate their wealth. He said: Destroy it.

c: Al-Muthanna told me, he said, Abu Hudhayfah told us, he said, Shabl told us, on the authority of Ibn Abi Nujayh, on the authority of Mujahid,
m: the same.

c: Al-Muthanna told me, he said, Ishaq told us, he said, Abdullah told us, on the authority of Warqa’, on the authority of Ibn Abi Nujayh, on the authority of Mujahid,
m: the same.

c: Muhammad bin Saad told me, he said, my father told me, he said, my uncle told me, he said, my father told me, on the authority of his father, on the authority of Ibn Abbas:
m: Our Lord, obliterate their wealth, meaning: destroy them and annihilate their wealth. As for his saying:
h
And harden their hearts
, he means: And seal them so that they do not soften or expand with faith, as:

c: Al-Muthanna told me, he said, Abdullah told us, he said, Muawiyah told me, on the authority of Ali, on the authority of Ibn Abbas:
m: And Moses said before he came to Pharaoh: Our Lord, harden their hearts so that
h
they will not believe until they see the painful punishment
. So God answered him, and prevented Pharaoh from believing until he was drowned, so faith did not benefit him.

c: Muhammad bin Saad told me, he said, my father told me, he said, my uncle told me, he said, my father told me, on the authority of his father, on the authority of Ibn Abbas:
m: h
And harden their hearts
, he says: And seal their hearts, until they see the painful punishment, which is drowning.

c: Al-Muthanna told me, he said, Abu Hudhayfah told us, he said, Shabl told us, on the authority of Ibn Abi Nujayh, on the authority of Mujahid:
m: h
And harden their hearts
, with misguidance. ... He said, Ishaq told us, Abdullah told us, on the authority of Warqa’, on the authority of Ibn Abi Nujayh, on the authority of Mujahid:
h
And harden their hearts
, he said: with misguidance.

c: Al-Qasim told us, he said, Al-Hussein told us, he said, Hajjaj told me, on the authority of Ibn Jurayj, on the authority of Mujahid,
m: the same.

c: It was narrated on the authority of Al-Husayn,
m: who said: I heard Abu Muadh, who said: Ubayd ibn Sulayman narrated to us, who said: I heard Ad-Dahhak say regarding His statement:
h
And harden their hearts
, meaning: He destroyed them as disbelievers. As for his saying:
h
They will not believe until they see the painful punishment
, its meaning is: They will not believe in the oneness of God and acknowledge His oneness until they see the painful punishment, as:

c: Al-Muthanna told me, he said, Abu Hudhayfah told us, he said, Shibl told us, on the authority of Ibn Abi Nujayh, on the authority of Mujahid:
m: They will not believe in God, in what they see of the signs, until they see the painful punishment.

c: Al-Muthanna told me, he said, Abdullah told us,
m: on the Surat Yunus 10:88 And Moses said, "Our Lord, indeed You have given Pharaoh and his chiefs splendor and wealth in the life of this world, our Lord, that they may mislead [others] from Your way. Our Lord, obliterate their wealth
h
and harden their hearts
so
h
they will not believe until they see the painful punishment

." authority of Warqa’, on the authority of Ibn Abi Nujayh, on the authority of Mujahid, the same. ... He said, Suwaid bin Nasr told us, Ibn al-Mubarak told us, on the authority of Ibn Jurayj, on the authority of Mujahid, the same.

c: Al-Qasim told us, he said, Al-Hussein told us, he said, Hajjaj told me, on the authority of Ibn Jurayj, on the authority of Mujahid,
m: the same.

c: Al-Muthanna told me, he said, Ishaq told us, he said,
m: I heard Al-Manqari say: So they will not believe, he said: He called down curses upon them. The Arabs differed about the position of believe. Some Basra grammarians said: It is in the accusative case, because the answer to the command is with the letter fa’, or it could be a supplication against them because they disobeyed. It has been reported that the one who said this statement used to say: It is in the accusative case, in apposition to his statement:
h
So that they may go astray from Your path

. Another of them said, and it is the saying of the grammarians of Kufa: Its position is in the subjunctive mood, based on the supplication of Moses, peace be upon them, meaning: so do not believe, as the poet said: Do not let what is hidden appear before your eyes, and do not meet me except with your nose downcast. Meaning: (May what is hidden not be spread out from between your eyes), (nor may you meet me), in the supplication.

x: Some of the grammarians of Kufa used to say: It is a supplication, as if he said: O God, so let them not believe. He said: If you wish, you can make it an answer to his question to him, because the question was issued in the form of a command, so you make: so let them not believe in the accusative case as an answer, and it is not easy. He said: It would be like the saying of the poet: Oh camel, go with a broad neck to Solomon, so that we may rest. He said: The answer is not in the supplication, because it is not a condition.

The correct statement about that is that it is in the place of a supplication, meaning: so do not believe. I chose that because what preceded it was a supplication, and that is His statement: Our Lord, obliterate their wealth
h
and harden their hearts
. So attaching His statement: so do not believe, since it was in the context of that, to its meaning is more appropriate and more fitting. As for his saying:
h
Until they see the painful torment
, Ibn Abbas used to say that its meaning is: Until they see the drowning. We have mentioned the narration from him regarding that from some of its aspects previously.

c: Al-Qasim told me, he said, Al-Hussein told us, he said, Hajjaj told me, on the authority of Ibn Jurayj, Ibn Abbas said:
m: And
h
they will not believe until they see the painful punishment
, he said: drowning.

evidence.text: Some of them read it as: So that they may lead people astray from Your path, meaning: so that they may lead people astray from Your path and turn them away from Your religion.
Others read it as: So that they may go astray from Your path, meaning: So that they may go astray from Your path, and deviate from the path of guidance.

x: This is report from God about His answer to Moses, peace be upon him, and Aaron’s supplication against Pharaoh, the nobles of his people, and their wealth. God Almighty says: God said to them: Your supplication has been answered, against Pharaoh, his people, and their wealth.
How was the answer attributed to two people, while the supplication was only from one person?

Even if the supplicant was one, the second was a believer, namely Aaron, and therefore the answer was attributed to them both, because the believer is a supplicant. And the people of interpretation said the same.
Who said that?

c: Muhammad bin Bashar told me, he said, Abd al-Rahman told us, he said, Sufyan told us, on the authority of Ibn Jurayj, on the authority of a man, on the authority of Ikrimah,
m: regarding his statement:
h
Your prayer has been answered
, he said: Moses was praying, and Aaron was saying Amen, so that is what he said:
h
Your prayer has been answered

. Some Arabists have claimed that Arabs address one person as if they were two, and he recited the following about this: I said to my friend, Do not rush us to pull out its roots and cut down the wormwood.

c: Ibn Wakee’ told us, he said, Zakariya bin Adi told us, on the authority of Ibn Al-Mubarak, on the authority of Ismail bin Abi Khalid, on the authority of Abu Salih, who said:
m: h
Your prayer has been answered
, he said: Moses prayed and Aaron believed.

c: Ibn Wakee’ told us, he said, my father and Zaid bin Habbab told us, on the authority of Musa bin Ubaidah, on the authority of Muhammad bin Ka’b, he said:
m: Moses called and Aaron responded to him. ... He said, Abu Muawiyah told us, on the authority of his sheikh, on the authority of Muhammad bin Ka’b, who said: Moses called and Aaron responded to him.

c: Al-Muthanna told us, he said, Abu Naim told us, he said, Abu Jaʿfar told us, on the authority of Al-Rabiʿ, on the authority of Abu Al-ʿAliyah, he said:
m: h
Your prayer has been answered

, he said: Moses prayed and Aaron believed. ... He said, Ishaq told us, Abd al-Rahman ibn Saʿd told us, and Abd God ibn Abi Jaʿfar told us, on the authority of Abu Jaʿfar, on the authority of al-Rabiʿ ibn Anas, who said: Moses prayed and Aaron said, Amen, and that is what he said:
h
Your prayer has been answered

c: Al-Husayn bin Yahya told us, he said: Abd al-Razzaq told us, he said: Al-Thawri told us, on the authority of a man, on the authority of Ikrimah,
m: regarding his statement: “He said:
h
Your prayer has been answered
,” he said: Moses was praying and Aaron was saying: Amen, so that is what he said:
h
Your prayer has been answered

c: Al-Qasim told us, Al-Husayn told us, Hajjaj told me, on the authority of Ibn Jurayj, who said, Ibn Abbas said:
m: h
Your prayer has been answered
, for Moses and Aaron. Ibn Jurayj said, Ikrimah said: Aaron responded to Moses’ prayer, so God said:
h
Your prayer has been answered
h
so be steadfast

c: Yunus told me, he said, Ibn Wahb told us, he said, Ibn Zayd said:
m: Aaron used to say Amen, and God said:
h
Your prayer has been answered
, so the Amen became a prayer, and he became his partner in it. As for his saying:
h
So be steadfast

, it is a command from God Almighty to Moses and Aaron to be steadfast and firm in their matter, from Pharaoh’s call to answer to the oneness of God and obedience to Him, until God’s punishment comes to them, which He informed them that He answered them in, as:

c: Al-Qasim told us, Al-Hussein told us, Hajjaj told me,
m: Ibn Jurayj said, Ibn Abbas said: So be upright, meaning carry out my command, and it is uprightness. Ibn Jurayj said: They say that Pharaoh remained forty years after this call. And His statement:
h
And do not follow the path of those who do not know

, meaning: And do not take the path of those who are ignorant of the truth of My promise, so that you hasten My judgment, for My promise cannot be broken, and My threat is descending upon Pharaoh, and My punishment is inflicted upon him and his people.

x: God Almighty says: And We crossed the sea with the Children of Israel until they crossed it, and Pharaoh pursued them, meaning: Pharaoh and his soldiers pursued them. It is said from it, I followed him and I followed him, which have the same meaning. Al-Kisa’i, according to what Abu Ubaid mentioned about him, used to say: If it is meant that he followed them in good or evil, then the statement is ataba’ahum with a hamza on the alif. If it is meant: he followed their traces, or: he imitated them, then it is from itba’ta, with a shaddah on the ta’, without a hamza on the alif. They transgressed against Moses and Aaron and those who were with them from their people from the Children of Israel, and they were hostile, meaning: and they attacked them. It is a source of their saying: So-and-so attacked so-and-so in injustice, he attacked him aggressively, like He invaded, he invades, he invades.

It was narrated that some of them used to read: Baghyan wa Adwan, which is also a source of their saying: Ada ya’du ‘udwan, like: Ala ya’lu ‘alwan. “Until drowning overtook him,” he says: until drowning surrounded him, and in the speech there is something omitted, it was omitted to mention it because of the indication of what appeared in the speech about it, and that is: So Pharaoh and his soldiers pursued them in oppression and aggression, in it (So We drowned him), until drowning overtook him. And His saying: He said, ‘
h
I believe that there is no god except the one in whom the Children of Israel believe

, and I am of the Muslims,’ God Almighty says, informing about what Pharaoh said when he was about to drown and was certain of his destruction: I believe, meaning: I acknowledge that there is no god except the one in whom the Children of Israel believe. There are different readings of this: Some of them read, and this is the general reading of Medina and Basra, that he with the opening of the alif of that he with the application of I believed in it, and its accusative with it.
Others read: I believed that he with a kasra on the alif of that he as the beginning of the report. This is the reading of the majority of the Kufians.

My opinion on this is that they are two readings with similar meanings, and whichever one the reader recites, he is correct. And the people of interpretation said something similar to what we said about that.

Who said that? Ibn Hamid narrated, Yahya ibn Wadh narrated, Musa ibn Ubaydah narrated, on the authority of Muhammad ibn Ka'b, on the authority of Abdullah ibn Shaddad, who said: Jacob and his sons gathered with Joseph, and they were seventy-two, and they left Egypt with Moses when they left, and they were six hundred thousand. When Pharaoh caught up with them and they saw him, they said: O Moses, where is the way out? We have caught up with him, and we were suffering from Pharaoh. So God revealed to Moses: Strike the sea with your staff, and it split apart, and each part was like a great mountain, and the sea dried up for them, and God uncovered the face of the earth, and Pharaoh came out on a black horse, on his color from blackness eight hundred thousand, in addition to their colors of beasts. And under Gabriel, peace be upon him, was a thin horse, and there was no other female among them, and Michael was leading them, and no man of them deviated from it except that he added him to the people.

When the last of the Children of Israel came out, Gabriel approached him and stuck to him. The horse smelled the scent of a female, but Pharaoh could not control his actions. He said: Go forward, for these people have no more right to the sea than you! Then Pharaoh pursued them, until they were the first to come out. He bumped into them and called out:
h
I believe that there is no god except the one in whom the Children of Israel believe
, and I am of the Muslims. And it was called out: Now, although you disobeyed before and were of the corrupters.

c: Muhammad ibn al-Muthanna told us, he said, Muhammad ibn Jaʿfar told us, he said, Shuʿbah told us, on the authority of ʿAtaʿ ibn al-Saʿib, on the authority of Saʿid ibn Jubayr, on the authority of Ibn Abbas - and on the authority of ʿAdi ibn Thabit, on the authority of Saʿid ibn Jubayr, on the authority of Ibn Abbas - he
m: said: “One of them traced it back to the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, and said: Gabriel used to put clay in Pharaoh’s mouth for fear that he would say: There is no god but God.”

c: Al-Husayn bin Amr bin Muhammad Al-Anqazi told me, he said, my father told us, he said, Shu’bah told us, on the authority of Ata’ bin Al-Sa’ib, on the authority of Adi bin Thabit, on the authority of Sa’id bin Jubayr,
m: on the Surat Yunus 10:90 And We took the Children of Israel across the sea, and Pharaoh and his soldiers pursued them in oppression and enmity until, when drowning overtook him, he said, "I believe that there is no god except that in whom the Children of Israel believe, and I am of the Muslims." authority of Ibn Abbas, on the authority of the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, who said: “Gabriel, peace be upon him, began to put - or stuff - clay into Pharaoh’s mouth, fearing that mercy would reach him.”

c: Ibn Hamid told us, he said, Hakam told us, on the authority of Anbasa, on the authority of Katheer bin Zadhan, on the authority of Abu Hazim, on the authority of Abu Hurairah, he said,
m: “The Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: Gabriel said to me: O Muhammad, if you could see me covering him and putting some of the dirt in his mouth, for fear that God’s mercy would reach him and he would be forgiven! He meant Pharaoh.”

c: Al-Muthanna told me, he said, Hajjaj told us, he said, Hammad told us, on the authority of Ali bin Zaid, on the authority of Yusuf bin Mihran, on the authority of Ibn Abbas:
m: “The Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: When God drowned Pharaoh, he said: ‘
h
I believe that there is no god except the one in whom the Children of Israel believe
.’ So Gabriel said: O Muhammad, if you saw me, I would take from the mud of the sea and put it in his mouth, for fear that mercy would reach him.”

c: Al-Muthanna told me, he said, Amr told me, on the authority of Hakam, he said, Shu’bah told us, on the authority of Ata’ ibn al-Sa’ib, on the authority of Sa’id ibn Jubayr, on the authority of Ibn Abbas, on the authority of the Prophet,
m: may God bless him and grant him peace, who said: “When Pharaoh said: ‘There is no god but God,’ Gabriel began to fill it with clay and dirt.”

c: Muhammad ibn Abd al-A’la told us, he said, Muhammad ibn Thawr told us, on the authority of Muammar, he said,
m: I was told by someone who heard Maimun ibn Mihran say about His statement:
h
I believe that there is no god except the one in whom the Children of Israel believe
, he said: Gabriel took some of the mud of the sea and struck his mouth with it - or he said he filled his mouth with it - for fear that God’s mercy would reach him.

c: Ibn Wakee’ told us, he said, Al-Husayn ibn Ali told us, on the authority of Ja’far ibn Burqan, on the authority of Maimun ibn Mihran, he said:
m: Ad-Dahhak ibn Qays delivered a sermon, praised God and extolled Him, then said: Pharaoh was a tyrannical slave who forgot the remembrance of God. When he was about to drown, he said:
h
I believe that there is no god except the one in whom the Children of Israel believe

, and I am of the Muslims. God said: Now, although you disobeyed before and were among the corrupters. ... He said, my father told me, on the authority of Shuʿbah, on the authority of ʿAdi bin Thabit, on the authority of Saʿid bin Jubayr, on the authority of Ibn Abbas: When Pharaoh was about to drown, Gabriel began to stuff dirt into his mouth, fearing that he would be forgiven. ... He said, Muhammad bin Ubaid told us, on the authority of Isa bin Al-Mughira, on the authority of Ibrahim Al-Taimi: That Gabriel, peace be upon him, said: I have not envied mercy for anyone among the children of Adam except Pharaoh, for when he said what he said, I feared that it would reach the Lord and He would have mercy on him, so I took some of the mud and foam of the sea and struck his eyes and face with it. ... He said, Abu Khalid al-Ahmar told us, on the authority of Umar ibn Yaʿla, on the authority of Saʿid ibn Jubayr, on the authority of Ibn Abbas, who said: Gabriel, peace be upon him, said: I stuffed his mouth with mud for fear that mercy would reach him.

evidence.text: There are different readings of this: Some of them read, and this is the general reading of Medina and Basra, that he with the opening of the alif of that he with the application of I believed in it, and its accusative with it.
This is the reading of the majority of the Kufians.
Abu Jaafar said: My opinion on this is that they are two readings with similar meanings, and whichever one the reader recites, he is correct.

x: God Almighty says, informing Pharaoh of the ugliness of his actions during his life, and his wrongdoing towards himself during his health, by his persistence in his tyranny, and his disobedience to his Lord, when he fled to Him in a state of His wrath upon him, and His punishment descending, seeking refuge in Him from His torment that was befalling him, when he called out to Him while the waves of the sea overwhelmed him, and the anguish of death overwhelmed him, I believe that there is no god except the one in whom the Children of Israel believed, and I am of the Muslims to Him, submitting in humility to Him, acknowledging servitude: Now, you acknowledge servitude to God, surrender to Him in humility, and devote divinity to Him, and you disobeyed Him before His vengeance descended upon you, so you angered Him against yourself, and you were among the corruptors on earth, turning people away from His path? Why don't you, while you are in a respite, and the door of repentance is open to you, acknowledge what you are acknowledging now?
God Almighty says to Pharaoh: Today We will place you on a high ground
h
with your body

, and those who deny your destruction will see you as a perishing creature, so that you may be a sign for those who come after you, meaning: for those who come after you among the people, a lesson from you, so that they may be deterred from disobeying God, disbelief, and striving to spread corruption on His earth. And al-Najwa is a high place above the surrounding land. From this, Aws bin Hajar said: He who is saved by his punishment is like he who is saved by his salvation, and he who is hidden is like he who walks on a treadmill. And the people of interpretation said something similar to what we said about that.
Who said that?

c: Muhammad bin Abdul A’la told us, he said, Al-Mu’tamir bin Sulayman told us, on the authority of his father, on the authority of Abu Al-Salil, on the authority of Qays bin Abbad and others, he said:
m: The Children of Israel said to Moses: Pharaoh has not died! He said: So God brought him out to them and they looked at him like a red bull.

c: Yaqub ibn Ibrahim told me, he said, Ibn Ulayyah told us, on the authority of Saeed al-Jariri, on the authority of Abu al-Salil, on the authority of Qays ibn Ubad, he said
m: - and he was one of the most knowledgeable people - or: the most recent people - about the Children of Israel, he said: So he told us that when the first of Pharaoh's soldiers reached the sea, the horses feared the flames. He said: And a thin horse appeared to one of them, and he smelled its scent - I think he said: - so he slipped away and I followed him. He said: So when the last of Pharaoh's soldiers were in the sea, and the last of the Children of Israel came out, he ordered the sea to close in on them. So the Children of Israel said: Pharaoh did not die, and he would never die! So God heard their denial of His Prophet, he said: So He threw him on the shore like a red bull, and the Children of Israel could see him.

c: Ibn Hamid told us, Yahya bin Wazeh told us, Musa bin Ubaidah told us, on the authority of Muhammad bin Kaab, on the authority of Abdullah bin Shaddad:
m: So today We will save you
h
with your body
, he said: (His body), his body, the sea threw him into it.

c: Al-Muthanna told me, he said, Abu Hudhayfah told us, he said, Shibl told us, on the authority of Ibn Abi Nujayh, on the authority of Mujahid:
m: So today We will save you
h
with your body
, he said:
h
with your body

c: Al-Muthanna told me, he said, Ishaq told us, he said, Abdullah told us, on the authority of Warqa’, on the authority of Ibn Abi Nujayh, on the authority of Mujahid,
m: the same.

c: Al-Qasim told us, he said, Al-Hussein told us, he said, Hajjaj told us, on the authority of Ibn Jurayj, on the authority of Mujahid,
m: the same.

c: Tamim bin Al-Muntasir narrated to us, he said: Yazid narrated to us, he said: Al-Asbagh bin Zaid narrated to us, on the authority of Al-Qasim bin Abi Ayoub, he said: Saeed bin Jubair narrated to me, on the authority of Ibn Abbas, he said:
m: When Moses crossed the sea with all those with him, the sea met them - meaning: Pharaoh and his people - and drowned them. Moses’ companions said: We fear that Pharaoh has not drowned, and we do not believe in his destruction. So he called upon his Lord, and He brought him out, and the sea cast him out, until they were certain of his destruction.

c: Bishr told us, he said, Yazid told us, he said, Saeed told us, on the authority of Qatada:
m: h
So today We will save you with your body that you may be a sign to those who come after you
, he said: Groups of the Children of Israel denied that, so God threw him on the shore of the sea for them to look at.

c: Muhammad ibn Abd al-A’la told me, he said, Muhammad ibn Thawr told us, on the authority of Muammar, on the authority of Qatada:
m: So that it may be a sign for those who come after you, he said: When God drowned Pharaoh, a group of people did not believe that, so God brought him out as a sign and a sermon.

c: Al-Hasan bin Yahya told us, he said: Abd al-Razzaq told us, he said: Ibn al-Taymi told us, on the authority of his father, on the authority of Abu al-Salil, on the authority of Qais bin Ibad,
m: or someone else, similar to the hadith of Ibn Abd al-A’la, on the authority of Muammar.

c: Ibn Wakee’ told us, he said, Abdullah bin Raja’ told us, on the authority of Ibn Jurayj, on the authority of Abdullah bin Katheer, on the authority of Mujahid:
m: So today We will save you
h
with your body
, he said:
h
with your body
. ... He said, Muhammad bin Bakr told us, on the authority of Ibn Jurayj, who said, I was told on the authority of Mujahid: So today We will save you
h
with your body
, he said:
h
with your body

c: Al-Qasim told us, Al-Hussein told us, Hajjaj told me,
m: on Surat Yunus 10:92
h
So today We will save you with your body that you may be a sign to those who come after you

. And indeed, many among the people, of Our signs, are heedless. the authority of Ibn Jurayj, who said: The Children of Israel denied the death of Pharaoh, so he threw him on the shore of the sea for the Children of Israel to see. He said: Red, like a bull.

x: Others said: You will save your body from the sea, so we will take it out of it.
Who said that?

c: Muhammad bin Saad told me, he said, my father told me, he said, my uncle told me, he said, my father told me, on the authority of his father, on the authority of Ibn Abbas,
m: regarding his statement:
h
So today We will save you with your body that you may be a sign to those who come after you
, meaning that God saved Pharaoh for the Children of Israel from the sea, and they looked at him after he had drowned.

x: What is the meaning of his saying:
h
With your body
? Is it permissible for him to be saved with something other than his body, so that the statement requires that it be said in it:
h
With your body
It was permissible for him to save him with his body alive as he entered the sea. Since that was permissible, it was said: So today We will save you
h
with your body
, so that it would be known that He would save him with the body without a soul, but dead.

And His statement: And indeed, many of the people are heedless of Our signs, God Almighty says: And indeed, many of the people are heedless of Our signs, meaning: of Our arguments and evidence that worship and divinity are exclusively for Us, are heedless, meaning: forgetful, they do not reflect on them, nor do they consider them.
God Almighty says: And We settled the Children of Israel in true dwellings. It was said: He meant by that the Levant and Jerusalem. It was said: He meant the Levant and Egypt.
Who said that?

c: Ibn Wakee’ told us, he said, Al-Maharibi and Abu Khalid told us, on the authority of Juwaybir, on the authority of Al-Dahhak:
m: A place of truth, he said: The places of truth, Egypt and the Levant.

c: Muhammad bin Abdul A’la told us, he said, Muhammad bin Thawr told us, on the authority of Muammar, on the authority of Qatada:
m: A place of truth, he said, God made them dwell in the Levant and Jerusalem.

c: Yunus told me, he said, Ibn Wahb told us, he said, Ibn Zayd said:
m: And We had certainly settled the Children of Israel in a place of truth, Ash-Sham: And he read: To the land which We had blessed for the worlds
r
(Al-Anbiya’: 71)
. And His saying:
h
And We provided them with good things
, means: And We provided the Children of Israel with lawful sustenance, which is good. And His statement:
h
And they did not differ until knowledge came to them

, God Almighty says: And these children of Israel to whom We did this action did not differ until what they knew came to them. That is because before the Prophet Muhammad, may God bless him and grant him peace, was sent, they were unanimous in the prophethood of Muhammad and in acknowledging him and his mission, not differing about him in the description that they found written with them. But when what they knew came to them, some of them disbelieved in it and some of them believed in it, and the believers in it among them were a small number. So that is His statement:
h
And they did not differ until what was known came to them
, whom they knew, a prophet of God, so He put knowledge in place of the known.

x: Some of them interpreted knowledge here as the Book of God and His revelation.
Who said that?

c: Yunus told me: Ibn Wahb told us: Ibn Zayd said
m: about His statement:
h
And they did not differ until knowledge came to them

, he said: Knowledge is the Book of God that He revealed, and His command that He commanded them with. Did they differ until knowledge came to them out of envy among themselves? The people of these desires, did they fight except for envy! He said: Envy has two aspects: the aspect of preciousness in this world and those of its people who fought over it, and envy in knowledge, seeing this one as ignorant and mistaken, and seeing himself as correct and knowledgeable, so he envies this one who is mistaken with his accuracy and knowledge. And His statement: Indeed, your Lord will judge between them on the Day of Resurrection concerning that over which they used to differ, God Almighty says to His Prophet Muhammad, may God bless him and grant him peace: Indeed, your Lord, O Muhammad, will judge between those of the Children of Israel who differed concerning you on the Day of Resurrection, concerning that over which they used to differ concerning My affair in this world, by admitting those of them who disbelieved in you into Hell, and those of them who believed in you into Paradise. So that is His judgment on that day concerning that over which they used to differ concerning the affair of Muhammad, may God bless him and grant him peace.

x: God Almighty says to His Prophet Muhammad, may God bless him and grant him peace: If you, O Muhammad, are in doubt about the truth of what We have chosen you for and revealed to you, that the Children of Israel did not differ about your prophethood before you were sent as a Messenger to His creation, because they find you written down among them, and they know you by the description with which you are described in their book in the Torah and the Gospel,
h
So ask those who read the Scripture before you

, from the people of the Torah and the Gospel, such as Abdullah bin Salam and others like him, from the people of truth and faith in you among them, not the people of lies and disbelief in you among them. And the people of interpretation said something similar to what we said about that.
Who said that?

c: Al-Qasim told us, Al-Hussein told us, Hajjaj told me, on the authority of Ibn Jurayj, who said, Ibn Abbas said
m: regarding His statement:
h
So ask those who read the Scripture before you

, he said: The Torah and the Gospel, those who met Muhammad, may God bless him and grant him peace, from the People of the Scripture and believed in him. He says: So ask them if you are in doubt that you are written among them.

c: Yunus told me: Ibn Wahb told us: Ibn Zayd said
m: about His statement:
h
And if you are in doubt about what We have revealed to you

, then ask those who have been reading the Scripture before you, he said: He is Abdullah bin Salam, he was one of the People of the Scripture. So he believed in the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace.

c: Al-Qasim told us, he said, Al-Hussein told us, he said, Hajjaj told me, on the authority of Ibn Jurayj, on the authority of Mujahid,
m: regarding his statement:
h
So ask those who read the Scripture before you
, he said: They are the People of the Scripture.

c: It was narrated on the authority of Al-Husayn ibn Al-Faraj
m: who said: I heard Abu Muadh say: Ubayd told us who said: I heard Ad-Dahhak say about His statement:
h
So ask those who read the Scripture before you
, meaning the people of piety and faith from among the People of the Scripture, who were at the time of the Prophet of God, may God bless him and grant him peace.

x: Was the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, in doubt that the report of God was the certain truth, to the point that it was said to him:
h
And if you are in doubt about what We have revealed to you
, then ask those who read the Scripture before you?
No, and this is what a group of scholars said.

c: Yaqub bin Ibrahim told me, he said, Hisham told us, on the authority of Abu Bakr, on the authority of Saeed bin Jubair,
m: regarding his statement:
h
If you are in doubt about what We have revealed to you
, he said: The Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, did not doubt and did not ask.

c: Ibn Wakee’ told us, he said, Suwaid bin Amr told us, on the authority of Abu Awana, on the authority of Abu Bishr, on the authority of Saeed bin Jubair,
m: regarding his statement:
h
And if you are in doubt about what We have revealed to you
, then ask those who have been reading the Scripture before you, he said: He did not doubt and he did not ask.

c: Al-Harith told me, he said, Al-Qasim bin Salam told us, he said, Hisham told us, he said, Abu Bishr told us, on the authority of Saeed bin Jubair,
m: and Mansur, on the authority of Al-Hasan, regarding this verse, he said: The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, did not doubt and did not ask.

c: Bishr told us, he said, Yazid told us, he said, Saeed told us, on the authority of Qatada,
m: regarding his statement:
h
If you are in doubt about what We have revealed to you
, then ask those who have been reading the Scripture before you, he mentioned to us that the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: I do not doubt and I do not ask.

c: Muhammad ibn Abd al-A’la told us, he said, Muhammad ibn Thawr told us, on the authority of Muammar, on the authority of Qatada:
m: h
If you are in doubt about what We have revealed to you
, then ask those who read the Scripture before you, he said: It has reached us that the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: I do not doubt and I do not ask.

x: What is the way to explain this statement, then, if the matter is as you described?

We have explained in more than one place in this book of ours that the Arabs permitted the saying of one of them to his slave: (If you are my slave, then submit to my command), and the slave who is commanded to do so does not doubt that his master who said that to him is his slave.

Likewise, the saying of one of them to his son: (If you are my son, then be dutiful to me), and he does not doubt that his son is his son, and that this is from their speech that is correct and widespread among them, and we mentioned that with its evidence, and from it is the saying of God:
h

And Surat Yunus 10:94 So if you are in doubt about what We have revealed to you, then ask those who have been reading the Scripture before you. The truth has certainly come to you from your Lord, so never be among the doubters. when God said, O Jesus, son of Mary, did you say to the people, Take me and my mother as gods besides God

(al-Ma’idah 5:116), and God, the Most High, knew that Jesus did not say that. This is from that, the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, did not doubt the truth of God’s report and its correctness, and God, the Most High, reminded him of that from His command, and He was aware, but He, the Most High, addressed him as his people addressed one another, since the Qur’an was revealed in their language.
As for his saying:
h
The truth has come to you from your Lord verse

, it is a statement from God that is the subject. God Almighty says: I swear that the certain truth has come to you from the report that you are a Messenger of God, and that these Jews and Christians know the truth of that, and they find your description in their books, So do not be among those who doubt, meaning: So do not be among those who doubt the truth of that. If someone were to say: This verse was addressed to the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, and what is meant by it is some of those who did not have sound insight into his prophethood, may God bless him and grant him peace, but who had shown faith with their tongues, alerting them to a place where they could know the truth of his matter, which would remove confusion from their hearts, as God Almighty said: “O Prophet, fear God and do not obey the disbelievers and the hypocrites.
Indeed, God is ever Knowing and Wise.” (al-Ahzab 33:1), it would be a statement whose validity is not proven.

And God Almighty says to His Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace: And do not be, O Muhammad, among those who denied God’s proofs and evidence, lest you be among those who lost their fortune and sold God’s mercy and pleasure for His wrath and punishment.
God Almighty says: Those upon whom the word of your Lord is incumbent, O Muhammad, is His curse upon them by His saying: Indeed, the curse of God is upon the wrongdoers
r
, so it was confirmed upon them. It is said: So-and-so has a right to such-and-such, if it is proven and obligatory for him. And His saying:
h
They will not believe
, even if every sign came to them, means:
h
They will not believe
in God’s proofs, nor will they acknowledge the Oneness of their Lord, nor that you are God’s Messenger.

And if every sign came to them, and admonition and lesson, and they witnessed it, until they witnessed the painful torment, just as Pharaoh and his chiefs did not believe when the word of your Lord came into effect upon them until they witnessed the painful torment, then he said: I believe that there is no god except that in whom the Children of Israel believe
r
(Yunus 10:90)

, when his words did not benefit him, so likewise those upon whom the word of your Lord came into effect from among your people, from the idol worshippers and others, they will not believe in you and follow you, except at the time when their belief will not benefit them. And the people of interpretation said something similar to what we said about that.
Who said that?

c: Al-Muthanna told me, he said, Abu Hudhayfah told us, he said, Shibl told us, on the authority of Ibn Abi Nujayh, on the authority of Mujahid,
m: regarding his statement: Indeed, those upon whom the word of your Lord has come into effect will not believe, he said: The wrath of God has come into effect upon them because they disobeyed Him.

c: Muhammad bin Abdul A’la told us, he said, Muhammad bin Thawr told us, on the authority of Muammar, on the authority of Qatada:
m: Indeed, those upon whom the word of your Lord has come into effect will not believe, God’s wrath has come into effect upon them because they disobeyed Him.

x: God Almighty says: Why was there not a city that believed? It is also mentioned in Abi’s reading. The meaning of the words: There was no village that believed when it witnessed the punishment and the descent of God’s wrath upon it, due to its disobedience to its Lord and its deserving of His punishment, and its faith benefited it at that time, just as Pharaoh’s faith did not benefit him when he was drowned after he persisted in his transgression and deserved God’s wrath due to his disobedience, except the people of Jonah, for their faith benefited them after the punishment descended and the wrath descended upon them. So God excluded the people of Jonah from the people of the villages whose faith did not benefit them after the punishment descended upon their courtyards, and He took them out of them, and He informed His creation that their faith benefited them in particular from among all the nations other than them.
If the matter is as you have described, that his statement:
h
Why was there not a village that believed and its belief benefited it

, means: Why was there not a village that believed, meaning denial, then how is a people in the accusative case, when you know that what comes before the exception is denial, what comes after it is in the nominative case, and that the correct speech of the Arabs is: No one stood up except your brother and No one went out except your father?

That is what is like that, if what comes after the exception is of the same type as what comes before it, and that is because (brother) is of the same type as (father), but if the two types differ so that what comes after the exception is not of the same type as what comes before it, then the eloquent of their speech is the accusative, and that is if you say: (No one remains in the house except the peg), and (We have no one except a dog or a donkey), because (the dog), (the peg) and (the donkey) are not of the same type as (one), and from it is the saying of Al-Nabigha Al-Dhubyani: I couldn't find an answer, and no one is here Then he said: Except that I hide it for no reason, and distance is like a pool that sheds light on the oppressed. So (al-Awari) was placed in the accusative case, since it was an exception from something other than its own kind. Likewise, (the people of Yunus) was placed in the accusative case, because they are a nation other than the nations from which they were excepted, and other than their kind and form, even though they were from the children of Adam. This exception, which some Arab scholars call the discontinuous exception, had (the people of Yunus) been part of (the nation) from which they were excepted, the statement would have been in the nominative case, but they are as described. And the people of interpretation said something similar to what we said about that.
Who said that?

c: Al-Qasim told us, Al-Husayn told us, Hajjaj told me, on the authority of Ibn Jurayj, on the authority of Ata’ Al-Khurasani, on the authority of Ibn Abbas,
m: regarding his statement:
h
Why was there not a town that believed and its faith benefited it

? He said: There was no town that believed and its faith benefited it when the punishment of God descended upon it, except the town of Yunus. Ibn Jurayj said, Mujahid said: There was no town that believed and its faith benefited it, as the faith of the people of Yunus benefited from it, except the people of Yunus.

c: Bishr told us, Yazid told us, Saeed told us, on the authority of Qatada,
m: regarding his statement: “
h
Why was there not a city that believed and its faith benefited it
, except the people of Jonah?
h
When they believed

, We removed from them the punishment of disgrace in the life of this world and gave them enjoyment for a time,” he says: This did not happen among the nations before them. It did not benefit a city that disbelieved and then believed when the punishment was about to come to it, and then it was left, except the people of Jonah. When they lost their prophet and thought that the punishment had drawn near to them, God cast repentance into their hearts, and they put on sackcloth, and separated every animal from its young, then they cried out to God for forty nights. So when God knew the sincerity in their hearts, and the repentance and regret for what had happened from them, God removed from them the punishment after it had descended upon them. He said: It was mentioned to us that the people of Jonah were in Nineveh, the land of Mosul.

c: Muhammad ibn Abd al-A’la told us, he said, Muhammad ibn Thawr told us, on the authority of Muammar, on the authority of Qatada:
m: Except the people of Yunus, he said: It reached us that they went out and camped on a hill, and separated every animal from its young, calling upon God for forty nights, until He accepted their repentance.

c: Ibn Wakee’ told us, he said, Abdul Hamid Al-Hamani told us, on the authority of Ismail bin Abdul Malik, on the authority of Saeed bin Jubair, who said:
m: The torment covered the people of Yunus, just as a garment covers a grave.

c: Al-Qasim told us, Al-Hussein told us, Hajjaj told me, on the authority of Salih Al-Mari, on the authority of Qatada, on the authority of Ibn Abbas:
m: The punishment descended upon the people of Yunus until there was only two-thirds of a mile between them and it. When they called out, God removed it from them.

c: Al-Muthanna told me, he said, Abu Hudhayfah told us, he said, Shibl told us, on the authority of Ibn Abi Nujayh, on the authority of Mujahid,
m: and Ishaq said, Abdullah told us, on the authority of Warqa’, all on the authority of Ibn Abi Nujayh, on the authority of Mujahid:
h
Why was there not a city that believed and its faith benefited it
, except the people of Yunus,
h
when they believed

, he said: As the people of Yunus benefited, Abu Hudhayfah added in his hadith, he said: There was not a city that believed when it saw the punishment and its faith benefited it, except the people of Yunus, we gave them enjoyment.

c: Al-Muthanna told me, he said, Ishaq told us, he said, Abdullah bin Abi Jaafar told us, on the authority of his father, on the authority of Al-Rabi bin Anas, he said,
m: a man who had recited the Qur’an in his heart, during the caliphate of Umar bin Al-Khattab, may God be pleased with him, told us about the people of Yunus when he warned his people and they denied him, so he told them that the punishment would befall them, and he left them. So when they saw that and the punishment overtook them, they left their homes and ascended to a high place, and that they cried out to their Lord and called upon Him, sincerely devoting their religion to Him: that He would remove the punishment from them and that their Messenger would return to them. He said: So about that, the verse was revealed: “
h
Why was there not a city that believed and its faith benefited it
, except the people of Yunus?
h
When they believed

, We removed from them the punishment of disgrace in the life of this world and gave them enjoyment for a time.” So there was no city that was overtaken by the punishment and then held back, except the people of Yunus in particular. When Yunus saw that, he went away blaming his Lord, and he set off in anger, thinking that He would not prevail over him, until he boarded a ship, and its people were struck by a strong wind, so he mentioned the story of Yunus and his report.

c: Al-Muthanna told me, he said, Abu Hudhayfah told us, he said, Shibl told us, on the authority of Ibn Abi Nujayh, he said:
m: When they felt the punishment was about to descend, they separated every female and her child from among the people and the livestock, then they all stood up and called upon God and made their faith sincere, and they saw the punishment being lifted from them. When the punishment was lifted from them, Yunus said: Go back to them, for you have lied to them! Yunus had promised them the punishment on a third morning, so at that moment he went out angry, and his opinion was bad.

c: Al-Harith told me, he said, Abdul Aziz told us, he said, Sufyan told us, on the authority of Ismail bin Abdul Malik, on the authority of Saeed bin Jubair, he said:
m: When Yunus was sent to his people, calling them to Islam, and he abandoned what they were doing, he said: He called them, but they refused. So it was said to him: Tell them that the punishment will come to them in the morning. They said: We have not found him lying, so look, if he spends the night among you, then he is nothing, and if he does not spend the night, then know that the punishment will come to you in the morning. So when it was the dead of night, he took three bags and took some provisions from them, then he went out. When morning came, the punishment covered them, as a man is covered by a garment in the grave. So they separated a man from his child, and an animal from its child. Then they cried out to God and said: We believe in what Yunus brought, and we have spoken the truth! So God removed the punishment from them. Yunus went out to look at the punishment, but he did not see anything. He said: They have found me lying! So he went, angry with his Lord, until he reached the sea.

c: Al-Qasim narrated to us, Al-Hussein narrated to us, Hajjaj narrated to me, on the authority of Israel, on the authority of Abu Ishaq, on the authority of Amr bin Maimun, who said: Ibn Masoud narrated to us
m: regarding the treasury, he said: Yunus, peace be upon him, had promised his people punishment, and he informed them that it would come to them in three days, so they separated every mother from her child, then they went out and cried out to God and asked His forgiveness. So God withheld the punishment from them, and Yunus went to see the punishment but did not see anything. And whoever lied and had no evidence was killed, so he went away in anger.

c: Ibn Hamid told us, Yahya bin Wadh told us, Salih al-Mari told us, on the authority of Abu Imran al-Joni, on the authority of Abu al-Jild Jilan, who said:
m: When the torment overtook the people of Yunus, they went to an old man from among the remaining scholars of theirs and said to him: The torment has descended upon us, so what do you think? He said: Say: O Ever-Living when there is no living, O Ever-Living, the Reviver of the dead, O Ever-Living, there is no god but You! So the torment was removed from them, and they enjoyed themselves for a time.

c: Muhammad bin Abdul A’la told us, he said, Muhammad bin Thawr told us, on the authority of Muammar, he said:
m: I heard in the letter of Ibn Masoud: Fulaula, meaning: Why not? And His statement:
h
When they believed
, We removed from them the punishment of disgrace in the life of this world, meaning:
h
When they believed
in their Messenger and acknowledged what he brought to them, after the punishment had overshadowed them Surat Yunus 10:98 So
h
why was there not a city that believed and its faith benefited it
, except the people of Yunus?
h
When they believed

, We removed from them the punishment of disgrace in the life of this world and gave them enjoyment for a time. and the command of God had enveloped them and the affliction had descended upon them, We removed from them the punishment of humiliation and disgrace in their life of this world, and We gave them enjoyment for a time, meaning: We delayed their appointed times and did not hasten their punishment, and We left them in this world enjoying their appointed times until the time of their death and the time of the end of their lives, which We had decreed to end.

x: God Almighty says to His Prophet: And if He had willed, O Muhammad, your Lord would have believed, all those on earth would have believed, in you, so they would have believed that you are My Messenger, and that what you have brought and what you are calling them to of the Oneness of God and sincere worship of Him, is true, but He does not will that, because it was decreed by God before He sent you as a Messenger that no one would believe in you, nor follow you and believe in what God sent you with of guidance and light, except for those for whom happiness was previously decreed in the first Book before the heavens and the earth and whatever is in them were created. And these are the ones who marvel at the truth of Our revelation to you of this Qur'an so that you may warn with it those whom I have commanded you to warn, from those who have already been decreed by Me that they will not believe in you in the previous Book.
And the people of interpretation said something similar to what we said about that.
Who said that?

c: Al-Muthanna told me, he said, Abdullah bin Saleh told us, he said, Muawiyah told me, on the authority of Ali, on the authority of Ibn Abbas,
m: his saying:
h
And if your Lord had willed
, those on earth would have believed, all of them together, “And it is not for a soul to believe except by permission of God,”
r

, and something similar to this in the Qur’an, for the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, was keen for all people to believe and follow him in guidance, so God informed him that no one believes except he for whom God has predestined happiness in the first mention, and no one goes astray except he for whom God has predestined misery in the first mention.

x: What is the point of his saying:
h
All of those on earth will believe
, since all indicates all, and all indicates all, so what is the point of repeating that, and each one of them is sufficient for the other?

The Arabs differed on this: Some of the grammarians of Basra said: He used the phrase both in this place as an emphasis, just as he said: Do not take two gods (al-Nahl 16:51). So in his phrase two gods is evidence of two.

Another said: He came with his saying: all together after all of them, because all together only occurs as an emphasis, and all of them occurs as an emphasis and a noun, so he came with all together after all of them. He said: If it was said that he combined them to show that their meaning is one, it would be permissible here. He said: Likewise: two gods (al-Nahl 16:51), the whole number is explained by it, so it is said: (I saw four people), so when he came with (two), and the number was sufficient from it, because they say: (I have one dirham and two dirhams), it is sufficient from their saying: (I have one dirham, and two dirhams), so if they said: (dirhams), they said: (three), because the plural is ambiguous, and (one) and (two) are not ambiguous, then the singular and dual were built on the structure of what is in the plural. Because it should be with each one, because (a dirham) indicates the type of which it is from, and (one) indicates all types.
Likewise (two) indicate all types, and (two dirhams) indicate themselves, so it came with numbers, because it is the origin. And His saying:
h
Would you then compel the people until they become believers

? God Almighty is saying to His Prophet Muhammad, may God bless him and grant him peace: No one will believe you, O Muhammad, and no one will follow you and acknowledge what you have brought except those whom your Lord wills to believe in you, not because you forced them, nor because you were keen on that.
h
Would you then compel the people until they become believers
