in you, believing in what you have brought them from your Lord? God Almighty is saying to him: So proclaim what you are commanded, and turn away from the polytheists upon whom the word of your Lord has come into effect that they will not believe.

God Almighty says to His Prophet: There is no way for a soul that You created to believe in you, O Muhammad, except by giving it permission to do so. So do not exhaust yourself in seeking its guidance, and convey to it the threat of God, and make it know what your Lord has commanded you to make it know, then leave it, for its guidance is in the hand of its Creator.
Al-Thawri used to say in his interpretation of his saying:
h
Except by the permission of God
, what:

c: Al-Muthanna told me, he said, Suwaid told us, he said, Ibn al-Mubarak told us, on the authority of Sufyan,
m: regarding his statement:
h
And it is not for a soul to believe except by permission of God
, he said: By the decree of God. As for His statement:
h
And He places defilement upon those who do not reason

, then the Most High says: Indeed, God guides whomever He wills of His creation to believe in you, O Muhammad, and He gives him permission to believe in you, so he believes in you, follows you, and acknowledges what you have brought from your Lord. And He places defilement, which is the torment and wrath of God, upon those who do not reason, meaning: those who do not understand from God His arguments, sermons, and signs by which He, the Most High, indicated the prophethood of Muhammad, may God bless him and grant him peace, and the truth of what he called them to of the oneness of God and the rejection of rivals and idols.

c: Al-Muthanna told me, he said, Abdullah told us, he said, Muawiyah told me, on the authority of Ali, on the authority of Ibn Abbas,
m: regarding his statement: And He makes the unclean, he said: wrath.

x: God Almighty says: Say, O Muhammad, to these polytheists among your people, who ask you for signs to prove the truth of what you are calling them to of the Oneness of God and the abandonment of rivals and idols: Look, O people, what signs are in the heavens that indicate the truth of what I am calling you to of the Oneness of God, from its sun and moon, and the alternation of its night and day, and the rain descending with provisions for the servants from its clouds, and in the earth from its ropes, and its cracking with its plants and the sustenance of its people, and all kinds of its wonders, for in that for you, if you understand and ponder, is a lesson and a lesson and an indication that this is from the actions of the One who cannot have a partner in His kingdom, nor does He have a back for His management and preservation, which suffices you from other signs. God Almighty says: And what do the signs and warnings avail a people who do not believe? God Almighty says: And what do the arguments, lessons, and messengers warning the servants of God against His punishment avail a people for whom God has already decreed misery, and for whom He has decreed in the Mother of the Book that they are among the people of the Fire? They do not believe in any of that nor do they affirm it, even if every sign came to them until they see the painful punishment.

God Almighty says to His Prophet Muhammad, may God bless him and grant him peace, warning the polytheists of his people of the imminent arrival of His punishment upon them, similar to what happened to their counterparts before them from all the nations that came before them, who followed the path of denying the Messengers of God and rejecting the Oneness of their Lord: Do these polytheists of your people, who deny what you have brought them from God, await, O Muhammad, anything but a day when they will witness from God’s punishment the same as the days of their ancestors who were upon the same polytheism and denial that they are upon, who passed before them and passed away from the people of Noah, Aad, and Thamud? Say to them, O Muhammad, if they are awaiting that: then await God’s punishment upon you, and the descent of His wrath upon you, for I am among those awaiting your destruction and ruin by the punishment that will befall you from God.
And the people of interpretation said something similar to what we said about that.
Who said that?

c: Bishr told us, he said, Yazid told us, he said, Saeed told us, on the authority of Qatada,
m: regarding his statement: Do they await anything but the like of the days of those who passed on before them? He says: God’s events with those who passed on before them, the people of Noah, Aad, and Thamud.

c: Al-Muthanna told me, he said, Ishaq told us, he said, Ibn Abi Jaʿfar told us, on the authority of his father, on the authority of Al-Rabiʿ bin Anas,
m: regarding His statement: Do they then await anything but the like of the days of those who passed on before them? Say, “Then wait, indeed, I am with you among those who wait. He said: He frightened them with His punishment, vengeance, and chastisement, then He informed them that if something like that happened, God would save His messengers and those who believed with him, so God said: “Then We will save Our messengers and those who believed. Thus is it incumbent upon Us to save the believers.”

x: God Almighty says: Say, O Muhammad, to these polytheists from your al-Nas 114:Wait for a time like the days of those who passed away before you from the previous nations who were destroyed by the punishment of God, for when that comes, no one will be destroyed by it except them and those who were like them in denying you, then We will save there Our Messenger Muhammad, may God bless him and grant him peace, and those who believed in him and confirmed his truth and followed his religion, just as We did before that with Our messengers whose nations We destroyed, so We saved them and those who believed in him with them from Our punishment when it was due upon their nations, Thus it is incumbent upon Us to save the believers, meaning: Just as We did with the previous ones from Our messengers, so We saved them and the believers with them and destroyed their nations, so We will do with you, O Muhammad, and with the believers, so We will save you and save the believers with you, incumbent upon Us without a doubt.

God Almighty says to His Prophet Muhammad, may God bless him and grant him peace: Say, O Muhammad, to these polytheists among your people who are amazed that I have revealed to you: If you are in doubt, O people, about my religion to which I call you, and you do not know that it is the truth from God, then I do not worship those you worship besides God, of the gods and idols that do not hear or see and do not avail me at all, so that you doubt its authenticity. This is an insinuation and a subtle tone of speech, but the meaning of the speech is: If you are in doubt about my religion, then you should not doubt it, but you should doubt what you are doing, which is the worship of idols that do not understand anything, and do not harm or benefit. As for my religion, you should not doubt it, because I worship God, who takes the creation and causes them to die if He wills, and benefits them and harms them if He wills.

That is because the worship of one who is like this is not denounced by anyone with a sound nature. As for the worship of idols, every person with a sound mind and intellect denounces it. And His saying:
h
But I worship God who takes your souls
, meaning:
h
But I worship God who takes your souls
and causes you to die at your appointed times. And I have been commanded to be among the believers, meaning: He is the One who commanded me to be among those who believe in what came to me from Him.
God Almighty says: And I was commanded to be among the believers, “and to establish,” and the second that is in apposition to the first that. What he means by his saying:
h
Set your face toward the religion

, is to set yourself upon the religion of Islam, upright in it, not deviating from it to Judaism or Christianity, or idol worship. And do not be among those who associate others with God, meaning: Do not be among those who associate others with God in the worship of their Lord, lest you be among those who are destroyed.

God Almighty says: And do not, O Muhammad, invoke, besides your God and Creator, anything that will not benefit you in this world or in the Hereafter, nor harm you in religion or in this world, meaning by that the gods and idols. He says: Do not worship them hoping for their benefit or fearing their harm, for they neither benefit nor harm. If you do, that, and invoke them besides God, then you will be among the wrongdoers, meaning: among those who associate partners with God and wrong themselves.

The Almighty says to His Prophet: And if God afflicts you, O Muhammad, with hardship or affliction, there is none who can remove that except your Lord who afflicted you with it, not what these polytheists worship of gods and rivals, And if He intends for you good, meaning: And if He intends for you ease or blessing and well-being and joy, there is none who can repel His favor, meaning: No one can stand between you and that, nor prevent you from it, nor deprive you of it, because He is the One in whose hand is ease and hardship, not the gods and idols, nor anything else, He afflicts with it whom He wills, meaning: Your Lord afflicts, O Muhammad, with ease and affliction, ease and hardship, whomever He wills and desires, of His servants, and He is the Forgiving, of the sins of those of His servants who repent and return from their disbelief and polytheism to faith in Him and obedience to Him, the Merciful, of those of them who believe in Him and obey Him, that He does not punish them after their repentance and return.

God Almighty says to His Prophet Muhammad, may God bless him and grant him peace, Say, O Muhammad, to the people, O mankind, the truth has come to you from your Lord, meaning: the Book of God, in which is an explanation of everything that people need in their religious affairs, So whoever is guided, meaning: whoever is upright and follows the path of truth, and believes in what came from God of explanation, is only guided for [the benefit of] himself, meaning: he is upright on guidance and follows the path for himself, so he seeks good for himself by doing that and no one else, And whoever goes astray, meaning: whoever deviates from the truth that came to him from God, and contradicts his religion and what he was sent with Muhammad and the Book that he revealed to him, is only led astray to his own detriment, meaning: for the misguidance of that person only brings upon himself, not upon others, because no one else is held accountable for that, and no one will be led to destruction by that misguidance except himself, and no bearer of burdens will bear the burden of another, And I am not a guardian over you. He says: I have no authority over you to straighten you out. Your affair is up to God, and He is the One who straightens whomever He wills among you. I am only a messenger conveying to you what I was sent to you with.

God Almighty says: And follow, O Muhammad, the revelation of God that He reveals to you, and His revelation that He sends down to you, so act according to it, and be patient with what befalls you in God's cause from the polytheists of your people of harm and hardships, and with what befalls you from them, until God decides His matter concerning them and you with a decisive action, And He is the best of judges, meaning: He is the best of judges and the most just of judges.

So God Almighty judged between him and them on the day of Badr, and killed them with the sword, and He commanded His Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, concerning those who remained of them to take the path of those of them who were destroyed, or to repent and return to His obedience, as:

c: Yunus told me, he said, Ibn Wahb told us, he said, Ibn Zayd said
m: regarding His statement: “And I am not a guardian over you. And follow what is revealed to you and be patient until God decides, and He is the best of judges,” he said: This is abrogated, until God decides, God’s judgment is to fight them, and His command to be harsh with them. The last interpretation of Surah Yunus, peace be upon him

notes.en: Al-Ṭabarānī transmitted it in al-Duʿāʾ (no. 1753) and al-Bayhaqī in al-Asmāʾ wa-l-ṣifāt (no. 58), through Sufyān. Al-Ṭabarānī transmitted it in al-Duʿāʾ (no. 1754) through ʿUthmān ibn ʿAbd Allāh ibn Mawhab from Mūsā as his statement. Al-Suyūṭī attributed it in al-Durr al-manthūr, 1/110, to ʿAbd al-Razzāq, ʿAbd ibn Ḥumayd, and Ibn al-Mundhir.

notes.en: He is Ḥurayth ibn ʿAnnāb al-Ṭāʾī. The verse appears in Nawādir Abī Zayd, p. 124; Ibn Qutaybah’s al-Maʿānī al-kabīr, 2/1048; and Lisān al-ʿArab, root n-ṣ-y, with some differences from the wording here.
notes.ar: هو حُرَيث بن عَنَّاب الطائى، والبيت فى نوادر أبي زيد ص 124، والمعانى الكبير لابن قتيبة 2/ 1048، واللسان (ن ص ى)، وفى هذه المصادر بعض الاختلاف عن ما هنا.

notes.en: Ṣ reads “why did you not inform”; T1, T2, S, and F read “why did you not deliver.”
notes.ar: في ص: "ألا آذنت"، وفى ت 1، ت 2، س، ف: "ألا أديت".

notes.en: Ṣ, T2, S, and F read “al-Mushaqqar.”
notes.ar: في ص، ت 2، س، ف: "المشقر".

notes.en: This is by Labīd ibn Rabīʿah. The verse is in his Dīwān, p. 156.
notes.ar: هو لبيد بن ربيعة، والبيت في ديوانه ص 156.

notes.en: M reads “I rebuked, so we said”; T1 reads “I rebuked, we said”; T2 and S read “if I rebuked, we said”; F reads “I relieved, we said.”

notes.en: Unpointed in Ṣ and F; M reads “we hasten.” Rayʿ means “returning” or “going back.” See Tāj al-ʿarūs, root r-y-ʿ.
notes.ar: غير منقوطة فى ص، ف، وفى م: "نريع"، والرَّيع: العود والرجوع. التاج (ر ى ع).

notes.ar: في الديوان: "نُهى" على غير لغة طيّ.

notes.en: Ṣ reads “nuhā and riḍā”; T1, T2, S, and F read “nahā and riḍā.”
notes.ar: في ص: "نُهى ورُضى"، وفى ت 1، ت 2، س، ف "نها ورضا".

notes.ar: في م: "أبنيت"، وفى ت 1: "اسب"، وفي ف: "أتيت".

notes.en: The manuscripts read “ibn.” The established wording agrees with the two source texts used for documenting the report. See al-Jarḥ wa-l-taʿdīl, 3/240.

notes.en: Saʿīd ibn Manṣūr transmitted it in his Sunan (no. 1056, Tafsīr section) through Khālid. See also Ibn ʿAbbās’s reading in Mukhtaṣar shawādhdh al-qirāʾāt, p. 61.
notes.ar: أخرجه سعيد بن منصور في سننه (1056 - تفسير) من طريق خالد به. وينظر قراءة ابن عباس في مختصر شواذ القراءات ص 61.

notes.en: Ṣ reads “we deem it permissible that you pass them”; T2 and F read “we deem it permissible that they pass them”; S reads “he deems it permissible that we pass them.”
notes.ar: في ص: "نستجيز أن تعدوها"، وفي ت 2، ف: "نستجيز أن يعدوها"، وفى س: "يستجيز أن نعدوها".

notes.en: Ṣ, T1, and S read “more severe after us”; M reads “more wicked after us.”
notes.ar: في ص، ت 1، س: "أشد بعدنا"، وفى م: "أشر بعدنا".

notes.en: Ṣ, T1, T2, S, and F read “your denial.”
notes.ar: في ص، ت 1، ت 2، س، ف: "تكذيبكم".

notes.en: T2 reads “they committed crimes”; F reads “they committed an outrage.”
notes.ar: في ت 2: "اجرموا"، وفى ف: "احترحوا".

notes.ar: في ص، ف: "يقولون".

notes.ar: في ت 1، ت 2، س: "بني".

notes.en: Tafsīr Mujāhid, p. 380; through Mujāhid, Ibn Abī Ḥātim in his Tafsīr, 6/1937.
notes.ar: تفسير مجاهد ص 380، ومن طريقه ابن أبي حاتم في تفسيره 6/ 1937.

notes.en: Ṣ, T1, T2, S, and F read “one of you.”
notes.ar: في ص، ت 1، ت 2، س، ف: "أحدكم".

notes.ar: في م: "بفعل".

notes.en: T2 and F read “hope.”

notes.ar: في م: "المطر".

notes.en: Tafsīr Mujāhid, p. 380; through Mujāhid, Ibn Abī Ḥātim in his Tafsīr, 6/1938. Al-Suyūṭī attributed it in al-Durr al-manthūr, 3/303, to Ibn Abī Shaybah, Ibn al-Mundhir, and Abū al-Shaykh.
notes.ar: تفسير مجاهد ص 380، ومن طريقه ابن أبي حاتم في تفسيره 6/ 1938، وعزاه السيوطي في الدر المنثور 3/ 303 إلى ابن أبي شيبة وابن المنذر وأبى الشيخ.

notes.en: Maḥāl means scheming and seeking to achieve an aim by stratagems. See Lisān al-ʿArab, root m-ḥ-l.
notes.ar: المحال: الكيد وروم الأمر بالحيل. اللسان (م ح ل).

notes.en: The verse is in Maʿānī al-Qurʾān, 1/460, unattributed to a poet.
notes.ar: البيت في معانى القرآن 1/ 460 غير منسوب إلى قائل.

notes.en: The plural of qaṭr, meaning rain. See Tāj al-ʿarūs, root q-ṭ-r.
notes.ar: جمع قَطر وهو: المطر. التاج (ق ط ر).

notes.en: Zajal means raising one’s voice, especially in melodious singing. See Lisān al-ʿArab, root z-j-l.
notes.ar: الزَّجَل: رفع الصوت، وخُص به التطريب. اللسان (ز ج ل).

notes.en: Ibn Abī Ḥātim transmitted it in his Tafsīr, 6/1939, through Muḥammad ibn ʿAbd al-Aʿlā. ʿAbd al-Razzāq transmitted it in his Tafsīr, 1/293, from Maʿmar.
notes.ar: أخرجه ابن أبي حاتم في تفسيره 6/ 1939 من طريق محمد بن عبد الأعلى به، وأخرجه عبد الرزاق في تفسيره 1/ 293 عن معمر به.

notes.en: ʿAbd al-Razzāq’s Tafsīr, 1/293. Ibn Abī Ḥātim transmitted it in his Tafsīr, 6/1939, from al-Ḥasan ibn Yaḥyā, from him.
notes.ar: تفسير عبد الرزاق 1/ 293، وأخرجه ابن أبي حاتم في تفسيره 6/ 1939 عن الحسن بن يحيى عنه به.

notes.en: This is the reading of Nāfiʿ, Ibn Kathīr, Abū ʿAmr, ʿĀṣim, Ḥamzah, and al-Kisāʾī. See al-Sabʿah, p. 325; al-Kashf ʿan wujūh al-qirāʾāt, 1/516; and al-Taysīr, p. 99.
notes.ar: هي قراءة نافع، وابن كثير، وأبي عمرو، وعاصم، وحمزة، والكسائي. ينظر السبعة 325، والكشف عن وجوه القراءات 1/ 516، والتيسير ص 99.

notes.en: This is also the reading of Ibn ʿĀmir. See the preceding sources and al-Nashr, 2/212.
notes.ar: وهى قراءة ابن عامر أيضا. ينظر المصادر السابقة، والنشر 2/ 212.

notes.en: See the earlier discussion at 1/155.
notes.ar: ينظر ما تقدم في 1/ 155.

notes.en: M reads “in it.”

notes.en: Ṣ, T1, T2, S, and F read “the conveying.”
notes.ar: في ص، ت 1، ت 2، س، ف: "البلاغ".

notes.en: The nominative reading is that of Nāfiʿ, Ibn Kathīr, Abū ʿAmr, Ibn ʿĀmir, ʿĀṣim according to Abū Bakr’s transmission, Ḥamzah, and al-Kisāʾī. The accusative reading is that of ʿĀṣim according to Ḥafṣ’s transmission. See al-Sabʿah, p. 325; al-Taysīr, p. 99; and al-Baḥr al-muḥīṭ, 5/140.
notes.ar: قراءة الرفع هى قراءة نافع وابن كثير وأبي عمرو وابن عامر وعاصم في رواية أبي بكر وحمزة والكسائي، وأما قراءة النصب فهى قراءة عاصم في رواية حفص. ينظر السبعة 325، والتيسير ص 99، وينظر البحر المحيط 5/ 140.

notes.en: Al-Suyūṭī attributed it in al-Durr al-manthūr, 3/304, to the compiler and Ibn al-Mundhir.
notes.ar: عزاه السيوطي في الدر المنثور 3/ 304 إلى المصنف وابن المنذر.

notes.en: Omitted in T1, T2, S, and F.

notes.en: The verse is in his Dīwān, p. 31.
notes.ar: البيت في ديوانه ص 31.

notes.en: M reads “to me.” It will also occur on p. 560.
notes.ar: في م: "لي". وسيأتي أيضا في ص 560.

notes.ar: في ت 2، س، ف: "يتناهون".

notes.en: Ṣ, T1, T2, S, and F read “it happened.” Ḥadiba ʿalayhi yaḥdabu means he showed him affection and concern. See Lisān al-ʿArab, root ḥ-d-b. The intended meaning is that he bent over it.
notes.ar: في ص، ت 1، ت 2، س، ف: "حدث" وحدِب عليه يحدَب إذا عطف عليه. ينظر اللسان (ح د ب). والمراد أنه انكب عليها.

notes.en: Ibn Abī Ḥātim transmitted it in his Tafsīr, 6/1941, through Saʿīd.
notes.ar: أخرجه ابن أبي حاتم في تفسيره 6/ 1941 من طريق سعيد به.

notes.en: Ibn Abī Ḥātim transmitted it in his Tafsīr, 6/1941, through Muḥammad ibn ʿAbd al-Aʿlā. ʿAbd al-Razzāq transmitted it in his Tafsīr, 1/293, from Maʿmar. Al-Suyūṭī attributed it in al-Durr al-manthūr to Ibn al-Mundhir and Abū al-Shaykh.
notes.ar: أخرجه ابن أبي حاتم في تفسيره 6/ 1941 من طريق محمد بن عبد الأعلى به، وأخرجه عبد الرزاق في تفسيره 1/ 293 عن معمر به. وعزاه السيوطي في الدر المنثور إلى ابن المنذر وأبى الشيخ.

notes.en: Ibn Kathīr mentioned it in his Tafsīr, 4/197, from the compiler. Al-Suyūṭī attributed it in al-Durr al-manthūr, 3/304, to the compiler.
notes.ar: ذكره ابن كثير في تفسيره 4/ 197 عن المصنف، وعزاه السيوطي في الدر المنثور 3/ 304 إلى المصنف.

notes.en: Ibn Abī Ḥātim transmitted it in his Tafsīr, 6/1942, through Muḥammad ibn ʿAbd al-Aʿlā. ʿAbd al-Razzāq transmitted it in his Tafsīr, 1/293, from Maʿmar.
notes.ar: أخرجه ابن أبي حاتم في تفسيره 6/ 1942 من طريق محمد بن عبد الأعلى به، وأخرجه عبد الرزاق في تفسيره 1/ 293 عن معمر به.

notes.en: This is an irregular reading. Al-Suyūṭī attributed the report in al-Durr al-manthūr, 3/304, to the compiler and Ibn al-Mundhir.
notes.ar: هي قراءة شاذة، والأثر عزاه السيوطي في الدر المنثور 3/ 304 إلى المصنف وابن المنذر.

notes.en: See this reading in Ibn Khālawayh’s Mukhtaṣar shawādhdh al-qirāʾāt, p. 61; al-Baḥr al-muḥīṭ, 5/143–144; and al-Muḥtasab, 1/311.
notes.ar: ينظر هذه القراءة في مختصر شواذ القراءات لابن خالويه ص 61، والبحر المحيط 5/ 143، 144، والمحتسب 1/ 311.

notes.en: T1 reads “his gardens”; T2 and F read “his sides.”
notes.ar: في ت 1: "جناته"، وفى ت 2، ف: "جنابه".

notes.en: Ibn Abī Ḥātim transmitted it in his Tafsīr, 6/1943, through Muḥammad ibn ʿAbd al-Aʿlā.
notes.ar: أخرجه ابن أبي حاتم في تفسيره 6/ 1943 من طريق محمد بن عبد الأعلى به.

notes.en: ʿAbd al-Razzāq’s Tafsīr, 1/293, from Maʿmar. Al-Dārimī, 1/18; al-Marwazī in al-Sunnah (no. 109); and al-Ṭabarānī (no. 4597) transmitted it through ʿAbbād ibn Manṣūr, from Ayyūb, from Abū Qilābah, from ʿAṭiyyah, from Rabīʿah al-Jurashī, from the Prophet ﷺ.
notes.ar: تفسير عبد الرزاق 1/ 293 عن معمر به. وأخرجه الدارمي 1/ 18، والمروزي في السنة (109)، والطبراني (4597) من طريق عباد بن منصور عن أيوب عن أبي قلابة عن عطية عن ربيعة الجرشي عن النبي.

notes.en: Ibn Abī Ḥātim transmitted it in his Tafsīr, 6/1943, through Saʿīd.
notes.ar: أخرجه ابن أبي حاتم في تفسيره 6/ 1943 من طريق سعيد به.

notes.en: Omitted in Ṣ, T2, S, and F.

notes.en: Ibn Abī Ḥātim transmitted it in his Tafsīr, 6/1942, through al-Ḥusayn. Al-Bayhaqī transmitted it in al-Shuʿab (no. 3412) through ʿAbbād ibn Rāshid. Aḥmad, 5/197 (al-Maymaniyyah edition), and al-Ḥākim, 2/444, transmitted it through Qatādah. Al-Suyūṭī attributed it in al-Durr al-manthūr, 3/304, to Abū al-Shaykh and Ibn Mardawayh.
notes.ar: أخرجه ابن أبي حاتم في تفسيره 6/ 1942 من طريق الحسين به، والبيهقى في الشعب (3412) من طريق عباد بن راشد به، وأحمد 5/ 197 (الميمنية)، والحاكم 2/ 444 من طريق قتادةَ به، وعزاه السيوطي في الدر المنثور 3/ 304 إلى أبي الشيخ وابن مردويه.

notes.en: Ṣ, T1, T2, S, and F read “Khallād.” See Tahdhīb al-Kamāl, 8/209.
notes.ar: في ص، ت 1، ت 2، س، ف: "خلاد". وينظر تهذيب الكمال 8/ 209.

notes.en: Ṣ, T1, T2, S, and F read “what is in it.”
notes.ar: في ص، ت 1، ت 2، س، ف: "ما فيها".

notes.en: Al-Ḥākim, 2/338, and al-Bayhaqī in al-Dalāʾil, 1/370, transmitted it through ʿAbd Allāh ibn Ṣāliḥ, from al-Layth, from Khālid, from Saʿīd ibn Abī Hilāl, from Abū Jaʿfar Muḥammad ibn ʿAlī ibn al-Ḥusayn, from Jābir ibn ʿAbd Allāh. Al-Suyūṭī attributed it in al-Durr al-manthūr, 3/304, to Ibn Mardawayh.
notes.ar: أخرجه الحاكم 2/ 338، والبيهقى في الدلائل 1/ 370 من طريق عبد الله بن صالح عن الليث عن خالد عن سعيد بن أبي هلال عن أبي جعفر محمد بن على بن الحسين عن جابر بن عبد الله، وعزاه السيوطي في الدر المنثور 3/ 304 إلى ابن مردويه.

notes.en: Ibn Khuzaymah in al-Tawḥīd, p. 120; Ibn Mandah in al-Radd ʿalā al-Jahmiyyah (no. 84); ʿAbd Allāh ibn Aḥmad in al-Sunnah (no. 471); al-Ājurrī in al-Sharīʿah (nos. 590, 591); al-Bayhaqī in al-Asmāʾ wa-l-ṣifāt (no. 666); and Ibn Abī ʿĀṣim in al-Sunnah (nos. 473, 474) transmitted it through Isrāʾīl. ʿAbd Allāh ibn Aḥmad in al-Sunnah (no. 470), al-Ājurrī in al-Sharīʿah (no. 589), and al-Bayhaqī in al-Iʿtiqād, p. 132, transmitted it through Abū Isḥāq.
notes.ar: أخرجه ابن خزيمة في التوحيد ص 120، وابن منده في الرد على الجهمية (84)، وعبد الله بن أحمد في السنة (471)، والآجرى في الشريعة (590، 591)، والبيهقى في الأسماء والصفات (666)، والسنة لابن أبي عاصم (473، 474) من طريق إسرائيل به، وأخرجه عبد الله بن أحمد في السنة (470)، والآجرى في الشريعة (589)، والبيهقي في الاعتقاد ص 132 من طريق أبي إسحاق به.

notes.en: T1 and S read “Numayr”; T2 reads “Namīr.” See Tahdhīb al-Kamāl, 14/23.
notes.ar: في ت 1، س: "نمر"، وفى ت 2: "نمير". وينظر تهذيب الكمال 14/ 23.

notes.en: Al-Dārimī in al-Radd ʿalā al-Jahmiyyah, p. 52, and Ibn Khuzaymah in al-Tawḥīd, p. 120, transmitted it through Abū Isḥāq.
notes.ar: أخرجه الدارمي في الرد على الجهمية ص 52، وابن خزيمة في التوحيد ص 120 من طريق أبي إسحاق به.

notes.en: Al-Lālakāʾī transmitted it in Sharḥ uṣūl al-iʿtiqād, 3/461 (no. 792), through ʿAbd al-Raḥmān; Ibn Khuzaymah in al-Tawḥīd, p. 120, and al-Lālakāʾī, 3/461 (no. 793), transmitted it through Sufyān.
notes.ar: أخرجه اللالكائي في شرح أصول الاعتقاد 3/ 461 (792) من طريق عبد الرحمن به، وأخرجه ابن خزيمة في التوحيد ص 120 واللالكائي 3/ 461 (793) من طريق سفيان به.

notes.en: ʿAbd Allāh ibn Aḥmad transmitted it in al-Sunnah (nos. 472, 1145) through Muḥammad ibn Jaʿfar.
notes.ar: أخرجه عبد الله بن أحمد في السنة (472، 1145) من طريق محمد بن جعفر به.

notes.en: T1 reads “Yazīd.” Both are correct: his name is Muslim ibn Nadhīr; it is also said Muslim ibn Yazīd, or Muslim ibn Nadhīr ibn Yazīd. See Tahdhīb al-Kamāl, 27/546.
notes.ar: في ت 1: "يزيد"، وكلاهما صواب فاسمه مسلم بن نذير، ويقال: مسلم بن يزيد، ويقال: مسلم بن نذير بن يزيد. ينظر تهذيب الكمال 27/ 546.

notes.en: Al-Lālakāʾī transmitted it in Sharḥ uṣūl al-iʿtiqād, 3/458 (no. 783), through Ibn Mahdī; Ibn Khuzaymah in al-Tawḥīd, p. 120; al-Ājurrī in al-Sharīʿah (no. 591); ʿAbd Allāh ibn Aḥmad in al-Sunnah (no. 473); and al-Lālakāʾī, 3/458 (no. 784), transmitted it through Isrāʾīl. Ibn Abī Shaybah, 13/381, and al-Dārimī in al-Radd ʿalā al-Jahmiyyah, p. 52, transmitted it through Abū Isḥāq. Al-Suyūṭī attributed it in al-Durr al-manthūr, 3/306, to Ibn al-Mundhir, Abū al-Shaykh, al-Dāraquṭnī, and al-Bayhaqī.
notes.ar: أخرجه اللالكائي في شرح أصول الاعتقاد 3/ 458 (783) من طريق ابن مهدي به؛ وابن خزيمة في التوحيد ص 120، والآجرى في الشريعة (591) وعبد الله بن أحمد في السنة (473)، واللالكائي في شرح أصول الاعتقاد 3/ 458 (784) من طريق إسرائيل به، وأخرجه ابن أبي شيبة 13/ 381، والدارمي في الرد على الجهمية ص 52 من طريق أبي إسحاق به، وعزاه السيوطي في الدر المنثور 3/ 306 إلى ابن المنذر وأبى الشيخ والدارقطني والبيهقى.

notes.en: Al-Lālakāʾī transmitted it in Sharḥ uṣūl al-iʿtiqād, 3/462 (no. 794), through Sharīk. Al-Suyūṭī attributed it in al-Durr al-manthūr, 3/306, to al-Dāraquṭnī.

notes.en: Al-Bayhaqī transmitted it in al-Iʿtiqād, p. 132, through Hawdhah. ʿAbd Allāh ibn Aḥmad in al-Sunnah (no. 1146) and Ibn Khuzaymah in al-Tawḥīd, p. 121, transmitted a similar report through al-Mubārak and ʿAwf, from al-Ḥasan.

notes.en: Al-Tirmidhī (nos. 2552, 3105) and Ibn Khuzaymah in al-Tawḥīd, p. 118, transmitted it through Ibn Bashshār. Aḥmad, 4/332 (al-Maymaniyyah edition), and Muslim (no. 181/297) transmitted it through Ibn Mahdī. In their versions it is connected, mentioning Ibn Mahdī, from Ḥammād ibn Salamah, from Thābit, from ʿAbd al-Raḥmān ibn Abī Laylā, from Ṣuhayb; this is the chain the compiler will cite next.
notes.ar: أخرجه الترمذي (2552، 3105)، وابن خزيمة في التوحيد ص 118 من طريق ابن بشار به، وأخرجه أحمد 4/ 332 (الميمنية)، ومسلم (181/ 297) من طريق ابن مهدى به، وهو عندهم موصول بذكر ابن مهدى عن حماد سلمة عن ثابت عن عبد الرحمن بن أبي ليلى عن صهيب، وهو السند الذي سيسوقه المصنف بعد ذلك.

notes.en: Ibn Mājah transmitted it (no. 187) through al-Ḥajjāj. Al-Ṭayālisī (no. 1411), Aḥmad, 4/332 (al-Maymaniyyah edition), Muslim (no. 181/298), al-Tirmidhī (no. 3105), al-Bayhaqī in al-Iʿtiqād, p. 128, and al-Asmāʾ wa-l-ṣifāt (no. 665), Ibn Mandah in al-Radd ʿalā al-Jahmiyyah (no. 83), al-Ājurrī in al-Sharīʿah (nos. 602–604), and others transmitted it through various routes from Ḥammād.
notes.ar: أخرجه ابن ماجه (187) من طريق الحجاج به، وأخرجه الطيالسي (1411)، وأحمد 4/ 332 (الميمنية)، ومسلم (181/ 298)، والترمذى (3105)، والبيهقي في الاعتقاد ص 128، وفي الأسماء والصفات (665)، وابن منده في الرد على الجهمية (83)، والآجرى في الشريعة (602 - 604). وغيرهم من طرق عن حماد به.

notes.en: T1 and S read “ʿImrān.” See al-Bukhārī’s al-Tārīkh al-kabīr, 3/517.

notes.en: Saʿīd ibn Manṣūr transmitted it in his Sunan (no. 1059, Tafsīr section); Ibn Abī Shaybah, 13/429; Ibn Abī Ḥātim in his Tafsīr, 6/1945; and al-Lālakāʾī in Sharḥ uṣūl al-iʿtiqād, 3/462 (no. 795), through Jarīr. Al-Suyūṭī attributed it in al-Durr al-manthūr, 3/306, to al-Dāraquṭnī.

notes.ar: هو أبو ذؤيب، وهذا صدر بيت في ديوانه ص 113 عجزه: *أحيى أبُوَّتَكِ الشُّمَّ الأماديحُ*

notes.en: The words in square brackets are an addition necessary to make the sentence coherent. See Lisān al-ʿArab, root z-y-l, and Maʿānī al-Qurʾān by al-Farrāʾ, 1/462.
notes.ar: ما بين المعقوفين زيادة لابد منها لاستقامة العبارة، وينظر اللسان (ز ى ل)، ومعانى القرآن للفراء 1/ 462.

notes.ar: هي قراءة ابن كثير ونافع وأبي عمرو وعاصم وابن عامر والكسائي. السبعة لابن مجاهدٍ ص 328. والتيسير ص 100.

notes.ar: هي قراءة حمزة وحده. السبعة لابن مجاهدٍ ص 328، والتيسير ص 100.

notes.en: Ibn Abī Ḥātim transmitted it, 6/1964, through Ibn Yamān, without mentioning Saʿīd ibn Jubayr. Al-Ṭabarānī (no. 12325), and through him Abū Nuʿaym in Akhbār Iṣfahān, 1/230–231, transmitted it through Yaḥyā ibn Yamān, from Ashʿath, from Jaʿfar, from Saʿīd. Al-Suyūṭī attributed it in al-Durr al-manthūr, 3/309, to Abū al-Shaykh, Ibn Mardawayh, and al-Ḍiyāʾ.
notes.ar: أخرجه ابن أبي حاتم 6/ 1964 من طريق ابن يمان، بدون ذكر: سعيد بن جبير، وأخرجه الطبراني (12325) ومن طريقه أبو نعيم في أخبار أصبهان 1/ 230، 231 من طريق يحيى بن يمان عن أشعث عن جعفر عن سعيد به، وعزاه السيوطى فى الدر المنثور 3/ 309 إلى أبى الشيخ وابن مردويه والضياء.

notes.ar: أخرجه ابن أبى الدنيا في الأولياء (26) من طريق زيد بن الحباب به، وأخرجه الطبراني (10476) من طريق زيد بن الحباب به مرفوعا. وينظر السلسلة الضعيفة (2409).

notes.en: Ibn Abī al-Dunyā transmitted it in al-Awliyāʾ (no. 15) through Yaʿqūb. Al-Nasāʾī in al-Kubrā (no. 11235), Ibn al-Mubārak in al-Zuhd (no. 218), al-Bazzār (no. 3626, Kashf edition), and Ibn Abī Ḥātim, 6/1964, transmitted it through Yaʿqūb with the addition of Ibn ʿAbbās as a Prophetic report. Al-Suyūṭī attributed it in al-Durr al-manthūr, 3/309, from Ibn ʿAbbās, to al-Ḥakīm al-Tirmidhī, Ibn al-Mundhir, Abū al-Shaykh, and Ibn Mardawayh.
notes.ar: أخرجه ابن أبي الدنيا في الأولياء (15) من طريق يعقوب به، وأخرجه النسائي في الكبرى (11235)، وابن المبارك في الزهد (218)، والبزار (3626 - كشف، وابن أبي حاتم 6/ 1964، من طريق يعقوب به بزيادة ابن عباس مرفوعًا، وعزاه السيوطى فى الدر المنثور 3/ 309 إلى الحكيم الترمذي وابن المنذر وأبى الشيخ وابن مردويه عن ابن عباس.

notes.en: Ibn Abī al-Dunyā transmitted it in al-Ikhwān (no. 5), and al-Bayhaqī in Shuʿab al-īmān (no. 8997), through Ibn Fuḍayl. Al-Nasāʾī in al-Kubrā (no. 11236) transmitted it through Muḥammad ibn Fuḍayl, from his father and ʿAmārah, from Abū Zurʿah. Abū Yaʿlā (no. 6110)—and through him Ibn Ḥibbān (no. 573)—transmitted it through Ibn Fuḍayl, from ʿAmārah, from Abū Zurʿah. Al-Suyūṭī attributed it in al-Durr al-manthūr, 3/310, to Ibn al-Mundhir, Abū al-Shaykh, and Ibn Mardawayh.
notes.ar: أخرجه ابن أبي الدنيا في الإخوان (5)، والبيهقى فى شعب الإيمان (8997) من طريق ابن فضيل به، وأخرجه النسائى فى الكبرى (11236) من طريق محمد بن فضيل عن أبيه وعمارة عن أبي زرعة به، وأخرجه أبو يعلى (6110) -وعنه ابن حبان (573) - من طريق ابن فضيل عن عمارة عن أبي زرعة به. وعزاه السيوطي في الدر المنثور 3/ 310 إلى ابن المنذر وأبى الشيخ وابن مردويه.

notes.en: Abū Dāwūd (no. 3527), Ibn Abī Ḥātim in his Tafsīr, 6/1963, and al-Bayhaqī in Shuʿab al-īmān (no. 8998) transmitted it through Jarīr. Abū Nuʿaym transmitted it in al-Ḥilyah, 1/5, through ʿAmārah. Al-Suyūṭī attributed it in al-Durr al-manthūr, 3/310, to Hannād and Ibn Mardawayh.
notes.ar: أخرجه أبو داود (3527)، وابن أبي حاتم فى تفسيره 6/ 1963، والبيهقي في الشعب (8998) من طريق جرير به، وأخرجه أبو نعيم في الحلية 1/ 5 من طريق عمارة به، وعزاه السيوطى في الدر المنثور 3/ 310 إلى هناد وابن مردويه.

Aḥmad transmitted it, 5/341, through Shahr. Maʿmar in his Jāmiʿ (no. 20324), Aḥmad, 5/342 (al-Maymaniyyah edition), Abū Yaʿlā (no. 6842), al-Ṭabarānī in al-Kabīr (nos. 3433, 3435), al-Baghawī in his Tafsīr, 4/139, and Sharḥ al-Sunnah, 13/50, and al-Bayhaqī in Shuʿab al-īmān (no. 9001) transmitted it through Shahr from Abū Mālik, without mentioning ʿAbd al-Raḥmān ibn Ghanm.
notes.ar: أخرجه ابن المبارك في الزهد (714)، وأحمد 5/ 343 (الميمنية)، وابن أبي الدنيا في الإخوان (6)، وابن أبي حاتم فى تفسيره 6/ 1963 من طريق عبد الحميد بن بهرام به. وأخرجه أحمد 5/ 341 من طريق شهر به. وأخرجه معمر في جامعه (20324)، وأحمد 5/ 342 (الميمنية)، وأبو يعلى (6842)، والطبراني في الكبير (3433، 3435)، والبغوي في تفسيره 4/ 139، وشرح السنة 13/ 50، والبيهقى فى الشعب (9001) - من طريق شهر عن أبي مالك بدون ذكر عبد الرحمن بن غنم.

Aḥmad, 5/321 (al-Maymaniyyah edition); Ibn Qāniʿ in Muʿjam al-ṣaḥābah (no. 689); and al-Ḥākim, 4/391, transmitted it through other chains from Yaḥyā.

notes.en: Sukkar, with ḍammah and doubled kāf, is a well-known sweet. It is an Arabized form of Persian shakar with fatḥah on both syllables. Sukkar is a fresh, pleasant fruit, a very sweet variety; also, grapes struck by a blight and scattered, leaving only a little of the cluster. They are fresh, intensely sweet, delicious, and white. See Tāj al-ʿarūs, root s-k-r.

notes.en: The source texts used to document the report read “you two hold us back.” Lisān al-ʿArab says: “His words, ‘Do not hold us back by uprooting its roots,’ mean: do not prevent us from roasting meat by pulling out the trees’ roots; instead, take what is readily available from their branches and twigs, and roast it for us quickly. Another version reads: ‘you two hold us back.’”

notes.ar: أخرجه أحمد في الزهد ص 34، وابن أبي حاتم في تفسيره 6/ 1989 من طريق صالح المري به، وعزاه السيوطى فى الدر المنثور 3/ 318 إلى المصنف وابن المنذر.

notes.en: ʿAbd al-Razzāq’s Tafsīr, 1/298, from Maʿmar. Al-Suyūṭī attributed it in al-Durr al-manthūr, 3/318, to the compiler and Abū al-Shaykh.
notes.ar: تفسير عبد الرزاق 1/ 298 عن معمر به، وعزاه السيوطى فى الدر المنثور 3/ 318 إلى المصنف وأبى الشيخ.

notes.en: The base manuscript adds: “The section has ended, and abundant praise be to God. Next, God willing, is the discussion of the interpretation of His saying, exalted is He: ‘Had your Lord willed, everyone on earth would have believed.’ From here onward, the numbering of manuscript T1 will be used as the base text.”
notes.ar: بعده في الأصل: "تم السفر والحمد لله كثيرًا، يتلوه إن شاء الله القولُ في تأويلِ قوله عز وجل: {وَلَوْ شَاءَ رَبُّكَ لَآمَنَ مَنْ فِي الْأَرْضِ}. وسيتم من هنا اعتماد أرقام المخطوط ت 1 أصلا في النص.

notes.en: M reads “but.”
notes.ar: فى م: "لكن".

notes.en: Omitted in M and F.
notes.ar: سقط مِن: م، ف.

notes.en: Ṣ, T1, T2, S, and F read “from what We have revealed to you confirming the truth of this Qurʾan.”
notes.ar: فى ص، ت 1، ت،2، س، ف: "من إيحائنا إليك صدق هذا القرآن"

notes.en: Ṣ, T1, T2, S, and F read “they pledge allegiance to him.”
notes.ar: في ص، ت 1، ت،2، س، ف: "يبايعوه".

notes.en: Omitted in Ṣ and T2.
notes.ar: سقط من: ص، ت 2.

notes.en: Omitted in Ṣ and S.
notes.ar: سقط من: ص، س.

notes.en: Ibn Abī Ḥātim transmitted it in his Tafsīr, 4/284 (no. 7250); al-Ṭabarānī in al-Kabīr (no. 13025); and al-Bayhaqī in al-Asmāʾ wa-l-ṣifāt (no. 139), through ʿAbd Allāh ibn Ṣāliḥ.
notes.ar: أخرجه ابن أبي حاتم فى تفسيره 4/ 284 (7250)، والطبراني في الكبير (13025)، والبيهقي في الأسماء والصفات (139) من طريق عبد الله بن صالح به.

notes.en: M reads “he did not praise.”
notes.ar: فى م: "لم يثن".

notes.en: M reads “thanāfī”; F, T1, and S read “tanāfī”; Ṣ is unpointed. The wording at this point is unclear, as though something has been omitted.
notes.ar: فى م: "ثنافى"، وفى ف، ت 1، س: "تنافى"، وفى ص غير منقوطة. والكلام في هذا الموضع غير مفهوم، فكأن ههنا سقطا.

notes.en: Ibn Abī Ḥātim transmitted it in his Tafsīr, 6/1990, through ʿAbd Allāh.
notes.ar: أخرجه ابن أبي حاتم فى تفسيره 6/ 1990 من طريق عبد الله به.

notes.en: M reads “admonition.”
notes.ar: في م: "موعظة".

notes.en: Ibn Abī Ḥātim transmitted it in his Tafsīr, 6/1991, through Saʿīd. Al-Suyūṭī attributed it in al-Durr al-manthūr, 3/318, to Abū al-Shaykh.
notes.ar: أخرجه ابن أبي حاتم في تفسيره 6/ 1991 من طريق سعيد به، وعزاه السيوطي في الدر المنثور 3/ 318 إلى أبى الشيخ.

notes.en: Ibn Abī Ḥātim transmitted it in his Tafsīr, 6/1991, through Ibn Abī Jaʿfar. Al-Suyūṭī attributed it in al-Durr al-manthūr, 3/318, to Abū al-Shaykh.
notes.ar: أخرجه ابن أبي حاتم في تفسيره 6/ 1991 من طريق ابن أبي جعفر به، وعزاه السيوطي في الدر المنثور 3/ 318 إلى أبي الشيخ.

notes.en: Omitted in Ṣ and M.
notes.ar: سقط من: ص، م.

notes.en: M reads “their communities.”
notes.ar: في م: "أممهم".

notes.en: Ṣ, T1, T2, S, and F read “it became due.”
notes.ar: فى ص، ت 1، ت 2، س، ف: "حقت".

notes.en: The manuscripts read “He harms whom He wills.” The adopted wording agrees with the context.
notes.ar: فى النسخ: "يضر من يشاء". والمثبت موافق للسياق.

notes.en: Ṣ, T1, T2, S, and F read “so not.”
notes.ar: فى ص، ت 1، ت 2، س، ف: فلا.

notes.en: Omitted in M, T1, T2, S, and F.
notes.ar: سقط من: م، ت 1، ت 2، س، ف.

notes.en: F reads “a human being.”
notes.ar: فى ف: "بشرٌ".

notes.en: Omitted in S.
notes.ar: سقط من: س.

notes.en: Ibn Abī Ḥātim transmitted it in his Tafsīr, 6/1993, through another chain from Ibn Zayd. See al-Naḥḥās’s al-Nāsikh wa-l-mansūkh, p. 529.
notes.ar: أخرجه ابن أبي حاتم في تفسيره 6/ 1993 من طريق آخر عن ابن زيد به، وينظر الناسخ والمنسوخ للنخاس ص 529.
